However, we also know that of the 36% of suffers, only 60% of the time is a defibrillator used.
Therefore, we must take 0.6 × 0.36 to find out how many patients are saved by the use of a
defibrillator.
This results in 0.216 or 22% of patients are saved by the use of a defibrillator.

questions.stem:
A paint company mixes its paint with water to create more paint per gallon. They currently have
ten gallon jugs which contain 10% water.
How much water must they add to create an 80/20 mix of paint to water?
questions.explanation:
Currently the mixture is 90% paint, 10% water or 9 gallons of paint for every 1 gallon of water.
For the company to create an 80% / 20% mix, the company must add 1.25 gallons to their
current 10 gallon mixtures. This will create 2.25 gallons of water for every 11.25 total gallons.
This results in a 2.25/11.25 or 20% water mix.

questions.stem:
A mail carrier can deliver mail to 1,400 different homes in one day. In the city of Utopia, there
are 52,800 residents.
How many mail carriers must be hired to deliver mail to all of the residents of Utopia each day?
questions.explanation:
To find the number of required mail carriers, simply divide 52,800 by 1,400 to get 37.714.
Therefore, you must round up and you have 38 mail carriers.

questions.stem:
How much change would you get back from a $100.00 bill if you purchased eight DVDs costing
$6.49 each?

Fencing costs $1.50 per picket. 2 pickets are used per foot. Posts cost $13.75 per post.
How much will it cost to fence a yard if 10 posts and 46 feet of pickets are needed?

Louis ran a race in 2.4 minutes. Laura ran the same race in 124 seconds.
What is the difference between the two times?
questions.explanation: 2.4 minutes is 144 seconds

questions.stem:
A grocery store has a special on sodas. Three 12 packs for $9.00.
How much does five 12 packs of soda cost?

A family of four have a dinner bill for $44.00. A 15% tip is added after an 8% tax is added to the
amount.
How much is the tip?
questions.explanation:
According to the question, this consumer added the 15% tip on top of the bill and the tax.
Therefore, you must first multiply $44.00 × 1.08 which equals $47.52. Now you will multiply

questions.stem:
Jane takes out a loan for $100,000.00 over 10 years and agrees to pay interest only at an
annual rate of 8%.
What will her monthly payment be?
questions.explanation:
This question is asking you to only determine the monthly payment of an interest only loan.
Thus, you do not need to concern yourself with the 10-year term or the principal being repaid as
that is irrelevant. The only numbers you need to work with are the principal amount, the interest
rate and the number of months in a year.
The formula for calculating an interest only loan would be (Principal × Annual Rate) / Number of
months in a year. Therefore:($100,000 × 0.08)/12 = $666.66666 or $666.67. A payment of
$666.67 per month would result in payments of $8000.04 per year which is 8% of $100,000.00.

questions.stem: The letter and numbers G78-15 printed on a tire refer to __________.

questions.stem: "Tracking," in terms of front-end alignment, means that __________.

options.A: each wheel travels independently of the other.
options.B: the wheels follow well on ice or in snow.
options.C: the front tires leave stronger tracks than the rear tires.
options.D: the rear wheels follow the front wheels correctly.

questions.explanation:
Tracking is correct when both rear wheels are parallel to, and the same distance from, the
vehicle centerline, which is an imaginary line drawn through the center of the vehicle. A bent
frame or twisted body structure will cause improper tracking.

questions.stem: A car with worn-out shock absorbers __________.

options.C: sags very low to the ground.
options.D: will have no traction on a wet road.

Shock absorbers control spring oscillation. Original equipment shocks that do not use air or
spring assists are not designed to control vehicle height.

questions.stem: In a three-speed transmission, the cluster gear is supported by the __________.

options.C: tighten to a specified torque, loosen five turns, and lock.

To properly adjust an automatic transmission band, loosen the adjusting screw locknut. Then
tighten the adjusting screw to the specified torque with a torque wrench. Next, loosen the
adjusting screw the specified number of turns. Complete the job by holding the adjusting screw
and tightening the locknut.

__________.

Spark plug leads must be installed in the correct tower of the cap to ensure the proper firing
order. The firing order is the order that the spark plugs ignite the air/fuel mixture in the
combustion chamber. A typical firing order for a six-cylinder engine is 1-5-3-6-2-4.

options.A: oxygen and acetylene to produce a flame.
options.B: oxygen and fluorine to produce a flame.
options.C: nitrogen and acetylene to produce a chemical reaction.
options.D: flux and acetylene to create an arc.

questions.explanation:
Gas welding uses an oxygen and acetylene mixture in a welding torch that produces a flame hot
enough to melt and fuse metals.

questions.stem: Tin snips are a type of __________.
questions.explanation:
The cutting blades of tin snips cut metal with a shearing action as they slide past each other.
The cutting blades of nippers come together and don't slide past each other. Tin snips have
nothing to do with either welding or measuring.

questions.stem: A combination wrench has __________.

options.A: an adjustable wrench on one end and an op en-end wrench on the other.
options.B: a box-end wrench on one end and an op en-end wrench on the other.
options.C: two box-end wrenches of successively larger sizes.
options.D: two op en-end wrenches of successively smaller sizes.

questions.explanation: A combination wrench has a box-end wrench on one end and an open-end wrench on the other.

questions.stem: Auger bits are used to __________.

options.A: make a dimple in metal to locate the bit as starts to drill.

questions.explanation: Auger bits are used to make holes in wood.

questions.stem: A carpenter's square is used to __________.

options.C: draw lines at right angles (90°) to each other.
options.D: draw lines at right angles (180°) to each other.

questions.explanation:
A carpenter's square is used to draw lines at right angles (90°) to each other. A level or spirit
level is used to tell if something is level or vertical; a plumb can also be used to tell if something
is vertical.

questions.stem: In arc welding, TIG stands for __________.
questions.explanation: In arc welding, TIG stands for Tungsten Inert Gas.

questions.stem: An Allen wrench __________.

options.A: is made exclusively by the Allen Manufacturing Company, LLC.
options.C: fits screws with an octagonal recess in the head.
options.D: fits screws with a hexagonal recess in the head.

questions.explanation: An Allen wrench fits screws with a hexagonal recess in the head of the screw.

questions.stem: A machine screw __________.

options.A: cannot cut threads in wooden surfaces.
options.B: is only used for steel building construction.
options.C: will work with any nut that has the correct diameter.
options.D: can be used to cut threads in sheet metal.

questions.explanation:
A machine screw cannot cut threads in wooden surfaces. Machine screws are used in a wide
variety of applications, not just building or construction; the diameter and pitch of the screw and
the nut must be the same for them to work together; and a machine screw cannot be used to cut
threads in sheet metal.

questions.stem: Uncontrolled, rapid drying of wood (for instance, lumber) causes __________.

options.B: harmless discoloration, unless it's green, which indicates rot

questions.explanation:
Uncontrolled, rapid drying of wood (for instance, lumber) causes checking and cracking. This is



why new lumber sometimes is kept submerged in water until it's time for it to be cut.

questions.stem: A finishing nail has a than a common nail __________.
questions.explanation: A finishing nail has a smaller head and smaller diameter than a common nail.

questions.stem: The piston of an internal combustion engine fits inside the __________.
questions.explanation:
The piston is the object inside the engine that moves up and down inside the cylinder to
produce the power needed.

questions.stem: The flywheel is attached to the __________.
questions.explanation:
The flywheel is used to keep the engine running smoothly inasmuch as it has a tendency to
smooth out the individual power surges generated by the various cylinders firing the fuel charge.
The flywheel is attached to the crankshaft.

questions.stem:
There are four types of fuel injection used in cars today. They are throttle body injection, multi-
port injection, direct injection, and __________.

options.A: a manual continuous electronic flow injection

questions.explanation:
The four types of fuel injection used in cars today are throttle body injection, multi-port injection,
direct injection, and sequential fuel injection.

questions.stem: Most automobile engines are __________.
questions.explanation:
Lawn mowers and outboard engines are two-cycle. They are used wherever horsepower is
needed in a lightweight package. They run very fast in order to produce power. Four-cycle
engines are used in automobiles, where various conditions exist and load variations are greater.
One exception is the rotary or Wankel engine, which uses a rotary design to convert pressure
into rotating motion instead of using reciprocating pistons.

questions.stem: When a spark plug fires, it is part of the __________.
questions.explanation:
The spark plug fires, driving the piston downward to produce power. The intake stroke allows
the fuel and air mixture to enter the cylinder. The compression stroke compresses the air/fuel
mixture. The exhaust stroke allows the burnt gases to be removed from the cylinder.

questions.stem: If the universal joints are broken and the car is standing still, the car will __________.

options.A: not move when the engine is revved up

questions.explanation:
Universal joints are needed to allow the drive shaft to flex when the car goes over a bump in the
road. If the universal joints are broken, the car will be unable to move since the drive shaft will
not be connected to the power source.

questions.stem: When the clutch is engaged on a manual transmission, the clutch pedal will be __________.
questions.explanation:
The clutch pedal is pushed to the floorboard in order to release the engine from the drive train.
Once the pedal is released and spring action returns it to the upward position, the clutch is
engaged and the engine is connected to the drive train again.

questions.stem: What gear is the transmission in when the engine is driving the car directly?
questions.explanation:
In a three-speed car first gear is used to get the car moving. Second gear is used to get it
moving a little fester.
Then it is placed in third gear when it has reached a higher speed and needs less power to
make it move even fester. When the third gear is engaged, no gear reduction is taking place
and the engine speed is reflected in the speed at which the wheels turn.

questions.stem: When the clutch is disengaged, the car will __________.
questions.explanation:
Disengaging the clutch means placing the car in neutral since the engine is disconnected from
the drive train.

questions.stem: A four-wheel vehicle driving on all four wheels is known as a __________.
questions.explanation:
A four-wheel vehicle is called a 4 × 4 if all wheels are driven. One with six wheels with all six
being driven is called a 6 × 6, and one with six wheels (like a truck) but only four being driven is
designated as a 4 × 6.

questions.stem: A squaring shear is used to __________.

options.A: cut metal off to a straight line.
options.C: fold a piece of sheet metal.
options.D: punch a piece of sheet metal.

questions.explanation:
A squaring shear is used to cut sheet metal - usually keeping it square to one edge if properly
aligned with the side of the unit. To shear means to cut.

questions.stem: If the engine will not start, the problem could be __________.

options.C: too much carbon in the drain holes or slots

questions.explanation: A weak battery is the first thing to check when the engine does not start or turn over.

questions.stem: When the mixture of fuel and air bums in the cylinder, it creates a temperature of __________.
questions.explanation:
When the mixture of fuel and air burns in the cylinder, it creates a temperature of 4000° to
4500°F.

questions.stem: The first emission control applied to automobile engines was called the __________.
questions.explanation:
The first emission control device for automobiles was the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV)
system.

questions.stem: A tire that bears the code "P 185/70 R 14" is __________.

options.A: a passenger-car tire that is 70 millimeters high.
options.B: a passenger-car tire that is 185 millimeters wide.
options.C: a radial tire that is 70 millimeters high.
options.D: a P-metric tire that is 70 millimeters wide.

questions.stem: In concrete work, to butter a concrete block means to __________.

options.A: put a finishing trowel to it

questions.explanation:
Buttering a concrete block means to put the mortar on it. This is usually done by taking the
mortar from the hawk and applying it to the block's edges.

questions.stem: On a woodworking plane, the "frog" refers to the __________.

options.A: handle on the rear of the plane
options.B: the sliding iron wedge that holds the plane iron at the proper angle
options.C: the opening at the bottom of the plane
options.D: the lever used to adjust the iron

questions.explanation: The frog is the sliding iron wedge that holds the plane iron at the proper angle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a softwood?
questions.explanation:
Softwood comes from conifers, or trees with needles, usually called evergreens. Such trees are
the pines, firs, and spruces.

questions.stem: To prevent rapid drying, freshly cut logs are often __________.

options.D: placed in sheds to dry slowly

questions.explanation:
Sometimes logs are not cut into lumber immediately and must be kept from checking and
splitting. This can be done by keeping them wet. At the sawmill the logs are kept floating in a



pond until they are about ready to be used. This way they do not dry out too quickly and check
or split.

questions.stem: A bumping hammer is used to smooth out dents by a(n) __________.
questions.explanation:
A collision auto repair worker uses a bumper hammer to take out some of the dents in a car's
sheet metal. This hammer is ideally suited for the job.

questions.stem: A groover is used to __________.
questions.explanation: A groover is designed to cause the seams to become flattened and make a watertight seal.

questions.stem: Sheet metal is formed into round cylinders by using a __________.
questions.explanation:
A squaring shear is used to cut sheet metal along a straight line. A bar folder is used to bend
sheet metal, and a punch press makes holes in sheet metal. The slip roll is used to form the
metal into round, cylindrical shapes.

questions.stem:
The tip of a soldering iron is coated with solder before it is used. This process of coating the tip



is called __________.
questions.explanation:
The tip of a soldering iron is tinned or coated with solder to make it more efficient in transferring
the heat at the tip to the object being soldered. It also prevents copper oxide buildup on the tip.

questions.stem: Punches are used in sheet metal work to __________.
questions.explanation:
Punches are used in sheet metal for the same reason punches are used elsewhere - to punch
holes.

questions.stem: A chisel is used for __________.
Which of the following items is used to measure angles?
questions.explanation:
A protractor is typically a half-circle made of metal or plastic that has tick marks spaced at one-
degree intervals around the edge.

questions.stem: Which system on an automobile uses shock absorbers?
questions.explanation:
The shock absorbers are the components in the suspension that dampen the vibrations in the
system.

questions.stem: Which automotive system uses universal joints, a drive shaft, and a clutch?
questions.explanation:
The clutch is used to engage and disengage the transmission. The drive shaft is used to
transfer power from the engine to the wheels. Universal joints are special linkages in the
transmission system.

questions.stem: Of which automotive system does the driver have the most direct control while driving?
questions.explanation:
The braking system can be controlled by the driver by pressing the brake pedal. The other
systems listed cannot typically be directly controlled while operating the automobile.

questions.stem:
Which of the following systems connects directly to the internal combustion engine in an
automobile?
questions.explanation:
The cooling system circulates water around the engine to prevent it from overheating. None of
the other systems is connected directly to the engine.

questions.stem: In the typical workshop, a plane is used for what purpose?
questions.explanation:
A plane is a hand tool that has a sharp blade extending slightly below the bottom surface of the
tool. The plane is pushed across the surface of a piece of wood and the blade removes a thin
layer of wood from the surface.

questions.stem: Which of the following woodworking objects would most likely be created with a lathe?
questions.explanation:
A lathe is a tool which is typically used to carve long, slender pieces of wood. The wood is
attached to the lathe and an electric motor spins the piece of wood. A cutting blade is then used
to remove parts of the wood, giving a decorative shape. A lathe would not be useful in making
the other objects listed.

questions.stem: The function of a catalytic converter is primarily to __________.

options.A: change pollutants into substances that are less harmful
options.B: improve the starting power of the automobile
options.C: force air into the engine for better acceleration
options.D: control the amount of gasoline that flows into the engine

questions.explanation: The catalytic converter converts pollutants into less harmful substances.

questions.stem: Which automotive system uses fuses and an alternator?
questions.explanation:
The fuses are used as links in the electrical system to prevent damage to other key
components. The alternator is used to recharge the battery when the car is running.

questions.stem: Which of the following items is part of the braking system is an automobile?
questions.explanation:
When the brake pedal is pressed, it operates the master cylinder, which forces the brake fluid
through the lines out to each wheel. The pressure in the brake lines causes the calipers to move
and press the brake shoes against the brake drum. This causes the automobile to slow down.

questions.stem: To make a wide groove in a board with a table saw, what type of blade would you use?
questions.explanation: A dado head blade is used for making wide grooves.

questions.stem: The function of a brake drum or rotor is to act as __________.
questions.explanation:
A brake system works on the principle of friction, which develops heat in the process of braking.
The drum absorbs and dissipates the heat developed.

questions.stem: The strongest bond for a wood joint would be __________.
A typical car engine has how many strokes per cycle?
What does "EFI" stand for in EFI computer?
When a driver presses the accelerator, the throttle __________.

options.A: breaks down to signal that maximum speed has been reached
options.C: remains neutral, as it has no connection to the accelerator
options.D: opens, which allows more air into the engine

questions.stem: The function of the tachometer is to __________.
Which of these is not a stroke?

Ron had his dad's permission to use his car, even though the predicted weather was frigid and
a snowstorm was expected. Ron remembered to check the oil and refill the cooling system with
water the night before he left. He also positioned the car near the end of the driveway so he
could easily get out if the snow started overnight. The next morning, the car started fine, but
steam began to come from under the hood after he had driven for a while.
What is the most likely cause of this?

options.A: He forgot to put the oil cap back on.
options.B: The engine is old and needs to be replaced.
options.D: He forgot to add antifreeze, as well as water, to the cooling system.

questions.stem: The purpose of the oil pump is to __________.

options.A: allow excess or dirty gas to be pumped out of the gas tank
options.B: lubricate the wheels to ensure they keep on rotating
options.C: reserve oil for the car to run in case the gas tank becomes empty
options.D: provide lubrication and prevent friction between metal parts of the engine

questions.stem:
If a driver inserts the key to start his car and finds that it does not work, then there is a problem
with the ignition system.
Seeing that the car has a full tank of gas, the next logical thing to do is __________.

options.A: replace the gas in the gas tank immediately
options.B: call a tow truck since there is no possible way of moving the car at that point
options.C: check the batteries by turning on the lights or radio
options.D: check to see if the wheels are flat

questions.stem: The __________ is the part of the electrical system in charge of absorbing excess current.
With an automatic transmission, which is the best  as to why is there no need for a clutch?

options.A: There is a torque converter that automatically changes the torque needed.
options.B: The clutch is responsible for the turning of the wheels but in automatic transmissions, it is replaced by the universal joint.
options.C: The clutch is already built into the accelerator.
options.D: The clutch is solely to change gears from 1-5. Automatic cars only use the D or drive gear.

questions.stem:
Joe loves to go on wild nature adventures. He always brings his four-wheel drive truck.
In difficult terrain such as deep snow or loose sand, why would Joe's truck do better than a 2-
wheel drive SUV?

options.A: It is capable of running faster on straight, dry pavements.
options.B: It can carry much heavier loads.
options.C: More driven wheels increase the likelihood of gaining traction.
options.D: The drive shaft extends from the transmission to the front axle.

questions.stem: The two types of brakes are __________.

The __________ is the emission-control system that forces unburned or partially-burned fuel
back into the cylinder in order to be burned.
The primary purpose of emission-control systems is to __________.
Generally speaking, a framing hammer is different from a mallet or a sledge in that __________.

options.A: framing hammers cannot be used to destroy or break surfaces
options.B: a framing hammer is the most difficult to control
options.C: framing hammers have softer heads than mallet and sledge hammers
options.D: a framing hammer has a claw to pull out nails

questions.stem: The fastening tool used to turn nuts and bolts is called a __________.
Which is not a real type of wrench?
The usual shape of the tip of a Phillips screwdriver is __________.
Another term for needle-nose pliers is __________.
The term for a pair of pliers made specifically for cutting wires is __________.
The crosscut saw has a unique shape and tooth angle enabling it to __________.
Which of these is not a cutting tool?
The significance of a saw having more teeth or points is that __________.

options.A: it can cut more efficiently on thick and rough surfaces
options.B: it can cut on smaller objects
options.C: it prevents the material being cut from breaking apart

questions.stem: The cold chisel called "cold" because __________.

options.A: it can cut metal without the need for a heat source
options.B: it is used in areas with colder temperatures
options.C: it is used to cut through giant blocks of ice
options.D: it is used to cut cold metal only

questions.stem: To bore holes into surfaces, a __________ is attached to a drill.

Phineas decided to build a tree house in the tree in his backyard. He had finished making the
walls and the roof and the last step was to put in the door, but he was having a difficult time
fitting it perfectly onto the door frame.
The door sides kept chafing on the door frame.
To fix this, he should ___________.

options.B: use a finishing tool (plane) to fine the sides of the door
options.C: make sure the wood material is intended for door purposes
options.D: varnish the sides of the door very well

questions.stem: Which of these is not a type of file?

The clamp used for holding things stationary, that has a screw which loosens and tightens the
clamp, is called a ___________.
The function of a wire gauge is to ___________.

options.A: measure if an old wire is still useable
options.B: determine the type of wire if it is undetermined
options.C: measure the electrical capacity of the wire

questions.stem: The two arms of a square are called ____________.

The material contained inside small tubes in levels to make sure that a surface is true or even
usually consists of ___________.

options.C: a type of liquid and an air bubble

questions.stem:
A square tests the accuracy of an angle. A level tests the evenness of a surface.
A plumb bob tests ____________.

The best type of nail to use when building a temporary wall that is certain to be torn down after a
while is the ____________.

ABS is a modern four-wheel system that prevents the wheels of the car from locking up. ABS
stands for __________.

Screws and bolts are types of fasteners which can be easily taken out of the wood surface with
little damage.
A screw with a square or hexagon-shaped head is called a __________.

The small, flat, metal item responsible for protecting the surface from the bolt digging into it and
additionally for keeping the bolt tight in place is called a ___________.
The tool used to back up a rivet is called a ____________.
When talking about nails, a 10d nail for example, the d stands for ____________.
A single row of cylinders in a car engine is called ___________.
The twisting force that causes rotation is properly referred to as __________.

Talking about the radiator, it is more common for a car to overheat during hot days than on cold
days because __________.

options.A: with direct sunlight, the cooling system does not work
options.B: the air that is supposed to cool the fluid or the coolant that flows through the radiator is not cool enough to do the job, hence overheating can happen
options.C: the radiator automatically shuts off when the outside temperature is too high
options.D: hot days have the tendency to melt the radiator

questions.stem:
The acoustical chamber that is part of the car exhaust system that lessens engine noise is
called __________.
The gauge that measures the electrical charge in a car is called the ___________.
The flow meter, a type of gauge, measures __________.

options.B: volume of flow in a piping system

questions.stem:
The tool that can be used to remove or tighten the spark plugs of an engine is called
__________.
In order to change a tire, a __________ must be used to lift the bottom of the car.

If a car has difficulty starting up, despite having a full tank of gas and no problems with the
electrical system, the next possible reason is because __________.

options.A: the battery is dead or missing
options.C: the air filter is very dirty
options.D: the pressure in the wheels is low

questions.stem: If a car starts but it does not move, there may be a problem with the __________.
A special type of ruler that has a half-moon shape to measure angles is called a __________.
Which of these is true regarding tire plies?

options.A: A "ply rating" tells you approximately how long the tire should last.
options.B: They connect the bead to the tread.
options.C: Plies can be radial, bias, or belted bias.
options.D: Their job is to protect the tire from curb impact.

questions.stem: If your car has a fuel injection system, which of the following will it not need?
questions.explanation:
A carburetor is not need with a fuel injection system since the fuel injection system forces the
gas/air mixture into each of the cylinders.

questions.stem: Which component distributes high voltage to the spark plugs?
questions.explanation:
The key term in the question is "distributes". A rotor is part of a car's distributor which distributes
high voltage from the coil to the spark plugs.

questions.stem:
Which type of bolt is has a square section that grips into the part being fixed (typically wood) to
prevent the bolt from turning when the nut is tightened?
questions.explanation:
A carriage bolt has a domed or countersunk head and a shank that is topped by a short square
section under the head.

questions.stem: What is the correct sequence of a four-stroke cycle gas engine?

options.A: intake stroke, compression stroke, power stroke, exhaust stroke
options.B: compression stroke, intake stroke, exhaust stroke, power stroke
options.C: intake stroke, power stroke, compression stroke, exhaust stroke
options.D: power stroke, compression stroke, intake stroke, exhaust stroke

questions.explanation: The correct sequence is intake stroke, compression stroke, power stroke and exhaust stroke.

questions.stem:
Which would be the last woodworking plane that you would use to prepare a rough sawn board
for finishing?
questions.explanation:
A typical order to use these planes to prepare a rough sawn board would be: scrub plane, jack
plane, jointer plane and smoothing plane.

questions.stem:
Which type of wrench is used to turn screw or bolt heads designed with a hexagonal socket
(recess) to receive the wrench?
questions.explanation: The Allen wrench is used to turn screws or bolts with a recessed hexagonal socket.

questions.stem: The best way to sand the end grain of wood is __________.
questions.explanation: The best way to sand end grain is crosswise.

questions.stem:
Which type of saw is best used for cutting small, often awkward features in building materials
such as drywall?
questions.explanation:
The keyhole saw has a long narrow blade and is often used to cut small openings in drywall and
other building materials.

questions.stem: Which component controls the amount of current that the alternator sends to the battery?
questions.explanation:
The regulator controls the output of the alternator to insure that the battery gets the proper
amount of current to keep it charged.

questions.stem: Which of the following will NOT occur from setting a spark plug gap wider?
questions.explanation:
Setting a spark plug gap narrower can result in a smaller weaker spark. Setting it wider may
result in a bigger spark, better combustion but a potential misfire.

questions.stem:
What should you do if your temperature gauge on your car indicates that the car is overheating
(in the red zone)?

options.A: Open radiator cap and pour in cold water immediately
options.B: Open radiator cap and pour in antifreeze immediately
options.D: Pull over and let the car cool down

questions.explanation: You should immediately pull over and let the car cool down.

questions.stem: Which of the following can cause water sludge in engine crankcase oil?
questions.explanation:
Water condensation in the crankcase is a leading cause of oil sludge. Changing your oil
frequently and using synthetic oil can help eliminate sludge.

questions.stem: Which of the following components prevents a car's battery from being overcharged?
questions.explanation: The voltage regulator controls the current that is sent to the battery to prevent overcharging.

questions.stem: Which of the following is probably NOT a cause of an engine overheating?
questions.explanation:
A faulty thermostat, inoperative fan motor and external coolant leaks can all cause an engine to



overheat.

questions.stem:
When you try and start an engine, you hear a clicking sound but nothing happens.
What is the potential problem?
questions.explanation: If you hear clicking but nothing happens, the problem could be the battery, solenoid or starter.

questions.stem: What type of wrench is pictured?
questions.explanation: The figure is a pipe wrench.

questions.stem: What type of clamp is this?
questions.explanation: The picture is a parallel clamp.

questions.stem: Which type of saw is designed to make accurate crosscuts at specific angles?
questions.explanation:
The miter saw is used from making accurate cross cuts and miter cuts.



Section 3: Electronic Information

questions.stem: Ohm's law states:
questions.explanation:
Ohm's law states that Voltage (V) = Current (I) × Resistance (R). All other answers are incorrect
expressions of this law.

questions.stem: Which of the following materials usually has an electromagnetic-induction device in its core?
questions.explanation: Iron is easily magnetized and demagnetized, so it works well for this device.

questions.stem: How many diodes should you expect to find in a bridge rectifier?
questions.explanation: A bridge rectifier is also known as a full wave rectifier, usually containing 8 diodes.

questions.stem: Another name for cycles per second is __________.
questions.explanation:
The number of times alternating current changes direction in one second is known as its
frequency, which is measured in hertz.

questions.stem: Newer cell phones contain a removable memory card, which is often called a __________.
questions.explanation:
SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module. The card contains information such as your phone
number, your billing information, and your address book. It makes it easier to switch from one
cell phone to another.

questions.stem: When current flows through a wire, the following influences are present __________.
questions.explanation: Voltage, ohms, and amperes are always present when current flows through a wire.

questions.stem: Millihenries are related to __________.
questions.explanation: Inductors are rated in millihenries.

questions.stem: Radar can operate at frequencies as high as __________.
questions.explanation: Radar can operate as high as 100,000 MHz (megahertz).

questions.stem: Radio waves travel __________.

options.C: faster than the speed of light
options.D: faster than the speed of sound but slower than the speed of light

questions.explanation: Radio waves travel at the speed of light. The speed of sound is much slower.

questions.stem: Changing alternating current to direct current is called __________.
questions.explanation: Changing AC to DC is a process called rectification.

questions.stem: Insulated fittings can be used to splice wires, thus eliminating the need for __________.

options.B: removing the plastic coating from the wires

questions.explanation: Insulated fittings replace soldering.

questions.stem: The symbol shown above stands for __________.
questions.explanation: This symbol stands for battery.

questions.stem: How many wires do serial cables used on computers have?
questions.explanation:
This is true, even if the cable has a 25-pin connector. Serial cables are often used to connect
computers to perpetual devices.

questions.stem: To produce greater storage of electrons and more capacitance, capacitors should __________.

options.C: have more voltage applied to them

questions.explanation: Connecting capacitors in parallel produces more capacitance.

questions.stem:
A light bulb is 60 watts.
Operated at 120 volts, how much current does it draw?
questions.explanation:
Power = Current × Voltage or, written another way, Current = Power/Voltage.



60 / 120 = 0.5 ampere.

questions.stem: A number-12 wire, compared to a number-6 wire __________.
questions.explanation: The larger the number, the smaller (in diameter) the wire.

questions.stem: A fuse with a higher-than-required rating used in an electrical circuit __________.
questions.explanation:
Because fuses are designed to prevent current overload at a specific level, a fuse with a high
rating may not work properly for a circuit rated at a lower level.

questions.stem: Neutral wire is always __________.
questions.explanation: Neutral wire is always whitish or natural colored.

questions.stem: To measure electrical power, you would use a(n) __________.
questions.explanation: Electrical power is measured in watts, so you use a wattmeter.

questions.stem: If you operate an incandescent light bulb at less than its rated voltage __________.

options.A: the bulb will burn brighter and last longer.
options.B: the bulb will burn dimmer and last longer.
options.C: the bulb will burn brighter but won't last as long.
options.D: the bulb will burn dimmer but won't last as long.

questions.explanation:
The bulb will burn dimmer because its full potential isn't used; it will last longer for the same
reason.

questions.stem:
Two electrical wires run to a machine. One wire is 6mm thick, and the other is 3mm thick.
For the two wires to carry the same current, the larger wire __________.

options.D: It can't be determined from the information given.

questions.explanation: Larger wires require less electrical pressure to run current.

questions.stem: Which of the following isn't a component of a DC motor?
questions.explanation: Rotor bars are found only on AC induction motors.

questions.stem:
A current passed through a muscle in the human body causes the muscle to contract.
This is known as __________.
questions.explanation: The ability of current to contracts muscles is called the physiological effect.

questions.stem: In a closed electrical circuit __________.

options.A: one terminal is always positive, and one terminal is always negative.
options.D: terminals are neither positive nor negative.

questions.explanation: In a closed circuit, one terminal is always positive, and the other is always negative.

questions.stem: What does RMS stand for?
questions.explanation: Root Mean Square is the peak value of voltage multiplied by 0.707 (sine 45).

questions.stem: The symbol above is a/an __________.
questions.explanation:
The symbol is a fuse. Fuses are designed to "blow" (melt) if the current flowing through it
exceeds a specified value.

questions.stem: The television broadcast standard used in the United States is __________.
questions.explanation:
NTSC stands for National Television Standards Committee. The system is also used in Japan.
PAL and SECAM are used in other countries.

questions.stem: The symbol above is a/an __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol is a lamp. A lamp is a transducer that converts electrical energy to light.

questions.stem: When a circuit breaker trips, in what position will you find the operating handle?

options.C: half way between on and off
options.D: three-fourths of the way between the on position and the off position

questions.explanation:
Conventional circuit breaker handles have four positions: on, off, trip, and reset. When tripped,
the handle moves to the middle position.

questions.stem: Which wire is smallest?
questions.explanation: The smaller the wire, the larger the number

questions.stem: The symbol above stands for __________.
questions.explanation:
The symbol stands for transformer. Transformers are used to step up (increase) and step down
(decrease) AC voltages.

questions.stem: How many paths of electrical flow can be found in a series circuit?

options.D: It can't be determined from the information given.

questions.explanation:
An example of a series circuit would be a string of Christmas lights. If you break the circuit's
path at any point, electricity will stop flowing and the lights will not work.

questions.stem:
A microwave is rated at 1,200 watts.
At 120 volts, how much current does it draw?
questions.explanation: I (current) = Power (watts)/Effort (volts). In this case, I = 1200/120 = 10 amperes.

questions.stem: Electricians use the term low potential to refer to __________.

options.A: electrical circuits with a low potential for overload
options.B: building codes that reduce the risk of fire
options.C: the likelihood of getting a raise this year

questions.explanation: Potential equals voltage; low potential is anything less than 600 watts.

questions.stem: Which of the following isn't a conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Glass is an insulator. Other insulators are plastics, paper, and rubber.

questions.stem: The ground wire is always __________.
questions.explanation: Ground wires are always green.

questions.stem:
To cause a current of 10 amperes to flow through 20-ohm resistance, the voltage needed is
__________.
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that V = IR. V = 10 × 20 = 200.

questions.stem:
Silver is a better conductor than copper. But copper is more often used because of



__________.

options.C: the low melting point of silver
options.D: the tendency of silver to tarnish

questions.explanation: Silver is a better conductor, but it's prohibitively expensive.

questions.stem: Electronic circuits that produce high frequency AC are called __________.
questions.explanation: Oscillators produce high-frequency AC.

questions.stem: If you plug an appliance designed for AC into a DC power source, the appliance __________.
questions.explanation:
When DC is applied to an AC appliance, the amount of resistance is less, so more current flows
through the wire and heat builds up.

questions.stem: What effect does a speaker wire's gauge have on speaker sound quality?

options.A: higher gauge wires are thicker with better sound quality
options.B: lower gauge wires are thicker with better sound quality
options.C: lower gauge wires are thicker with lesser sound quality
options.D: hire gauge wires are thicker with lesser sound quality

questions.explanation:
Unless a specific gauge is specified by the speaker manufacturer, you should always choose
lower gauges for better sound quality.

questions.stem: What's the primary advantage of a quad band cell phone over a dual-band cell phone?
questions.explanation:
There are four frequency bands used throughout the world. A quad-cell phone would be able to
access any of these frequency bands.

questions.stem:
When working with electricity, you should assume that all electrical equipment is alive unless
you know for certain otherwise.
This prevents __________.
questions.explanation: The greatest concern when dealing with electricity is personal injury.

questions.stem: The heat effect of current is created __________.

options.A: when the pressure of the current in the wire breaks up impurities in the wire, creating heat.
options.B: when the current in the wire decays electrons, causing them to move more quickly, creating heat.
options.C: when the current overcomes resistance in the wire, creating heat.
options.D: The heat effect of current is only theoretical; it has never been proven to exist.

questions.explanation:
Heat effect occurs when electrical current must overcome the resistance of the wire. Heat effect
can be quite obvious or very subtle.

questions.stem: What special type of diode is commonly used to regulate voltage?
questions.explanation: Zener diodes are available in a variety of voltages.

questions.stem: This symbol means __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol stands for ohm.

questions.stem: Electromotive force is another way of saying __________.
questions.explanation: Electromotive force is the pressure of the current, so the term is another way of saying voltage.

questions.stem:
A primary advantage of using a Li-Ion battery instead of a NiMH battery in your cell phone is
__________.

options.C: Li-Ion batteries don't interfere with signal quality

questions.explanation: Lithium-Ion batteries are much lighter than Nickel Metal Hydride batteries.

questions.stem: Transistors contain at least three terminals called the __________.

options.B: base, positive terminal, and negative terminal

questions.explanation: The three terminals a transistor must have are the base, emitter, and collector.

questions.stem: To control a light fixture from two different wall switches, you should use __________.

options.A: a single-pole switch and a four-way switch

questions.explanation: To control a light fixture from two different positions, use two three-way switches.

questions.stem: A transistor is also called a __________.
questions.explanation: Crystal amplifier is another name for transistor.

questions.stem: This symbol means __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol means ground.

questions.stem: To decrease capacitance, capacitors __________.

options.A: should have less voltage applied to them

questions.explanation: Capacitors connected in series reduce the amount of capacitance.

questions.stem: A resistor marked 2.5K ohms has the value of __________.
questions.explanation: 2.5K ohms is 2,500 ohms. K = one kilo or 1,000.

questions.stem: A 9-volt transistor contains __________.
questions.explanation: A cell is equal to about 1.5 volts, so 9 ÷ 1.5 = 6.

questions.stem: The hot wire is always __________.
questions.explanation: Live wires are black.

questions.stem: How wide is the full AT motherboard?
questions.explanation:
A motherboard is the physical arrangement in a computer that contains the computer's basic
circuitry and components.

questions.stem: The above symbol represents a/an __________.
questions.explanation: An on-off switch allows current to flow only when it's in the closed (on) position.

questions.stem:
If a 120-volt current is protected by a 25-amp circuit breaker, what's the largest number of watts
an appliance can safely use?
questions.explanation:
Determine the wattage that could cause the circuit breaker to trip with this formula:
Watts = Amperes × Volts or 25 × 120 = 3,000 watts.

questions.stem: The above symbol represents a __________.
questions.explanation: This type of variable resister is usually used to control voltage.

questions.stem: 16-gauge wire is __________________ than 12-gauge wire.
questions.explanation: 16-gauge wire is thinner than 12-gauge wire - the larger the gauge number, the thinner the wire.

questions.stem:
A 120-volt circuit has a resistance of 12 ohms.
How much current is present in the circuit?
questions.explanation:
A 120-volt circuit has a resistance of 12 ohms. A current of 10 amperes is flowing through the
circuit (120 volts divided by 12 ohms = 10 amps).

questions.stem:
When the secondary side of a transformer has more turns than the primary side, the output
voltage will be ___________ the input voltage.
questions.explanation:
When the secondary side of a transformer has more turns than the primary side, the output
voltage will be higher than the input voltage.

questions.stem: How much power is being carried in a 220-volt circuit when the current is 10 amps?
questions.explanation:
How much power is being carried in a 220-volt circuit when the current is 10 amps? 2,200 watts
(220 volts multiplied by 10 amps = 2,200 watts).

questions.stem: Capacitors connected in parallel __________.

options.C: are capable of handling more voltage.

questions.explanation:
Capacitors connected in parallel effectively increase the plate area, which allows for more
storage of electrons and more capacity or capacitance.

questions.stem: Another name for a transistor is __________.
questions.explanation:
The word "transistor" is a shortening of the term "transfer resistor". The transistor's original
name when it was invented in 1933 was the "crystal amplifier".

questions.stem: Current that changes polarity many times per second is called __________.
questions.explanation: Current that changes polarity many times per second is called alternating current.

questions.stem: The measurement "mil" refers to __________.
questions.explanation: A "mil" (from milli) refers to one thousandth.

questions.stem: A filter is used in a power supply to __________.

options.A: convert alternating current to direct current.
options.B: change direct current to alternating current.

questions.explanation:
A filter is placed in the power supply to even out any voltage variations. In some cases, a choke
may be used in the filter to smooth out the current variations.

questions.stem: Which of the following contains an electromagnet?
questions.explanation: Of the items listed, only a doorbell contains an electromagnet.

questions.stem: Radio frequency amplifiers are used in __________.
questions.explanation:
Radio frequency amplifiers are used in receivers and transmitters to amplify frequencies above
the range of sounds audible to humans.

questions.stem: A crystal microphone uses __________.
questions.explanation:
A crystal microphone relies on the piezoelectric effect, where a pressure on a crystal produces
an electric current.

questions.stem:
If both the resistors shown (R1 and R2) in the diagram below are of equal size, what is the
voltage at the arrow?
questions.explanation:
The total voltage drop of the circuit must equal the voltage across the battery, which is 24V.
Because the resistors are both the same size, each resistor creates half of the total voltage
drop: 24/2 = 12. Therefore, the voltage at the arrow is 12V.

questions.stem: A crossover network is used to __________.

options.A: direct the proper frequency range to the right speaker

questions.explanation:
A crossover network is designed to make sure that the right frequencies get to a speaker so it
can reproduce them better.

questions.stem: The klystron is used in __________.
questions.explanation:
The klystron is used as a frequency source in microwave units - from a microwave oven for the
kitchen to a radar unit for an aircraft

questions.stem:
The two basic types of oscillators used for microwave generation are the magnetron and the
__________.
questions.explanation:
The two basic types of oscillators used in microwave installations are the klystron and the
magnetron.

questions.stem:
The two types of diodes used in electronics work are the semiconductor diode and the
__________.
questions.explanation:
The two general types of diodes are the semiconductor and the vacuum tube diode. Both types



have their own particular applications and advantages.

questions.stem:
Analog color television relies on three colors to produce the full color range needed for a good
picture: red, blue, and __________.
questions.explanation:
Color television uses red, blue, and green "guns" to direct electron streams toward the
phosphors in the front of the picture tube, producing the full color spectrum when combined
properly.

questions.stem: The folded dipole antenna has an impedance of __________.
questions.explanation:
The folded dipole antenna - the one most commonly used for home TV reception - has an
impedance of 300 ohms. The dipole has an impedance of 72 ohms.

questions.stem: The symbol below is used in electrical diagrams to represent a __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol below is used in electrical diagrams to represent a capacitor.

questions.stem: Electricity is defined as __________.

options.A: the flow of electrons along a conductor
options.B: the flow of ions along a conductor

questions.stem: A conductor is any material that __________.
questions.explanation:
Conductors have free electrons that are easily moved along with the right kind of push or force.
There are a number of ways to cause these electrons to progress along a conductor. Heat, light,
magnetism, chemicals, pressure, and friction can cause the generation of an EMF useful in
causing electrons to move along a conductor.

questions.stem: Convention current flow is from __________.
questions.explanation:
Conventional current flow is said to be from + to -. This idea was originally used by Ben Franklin
to explain the conduct of lightning. This conventional flow is still used today by electrical
engineers and people working in physics.

questions.stem: Electron flow is from __________.
questions.explanation:
Electron flow can be demonstrated to flow from - to +. The action that takes place in a vacuum
tube indicates that the + attracts the - electron to cause it to move from - to +.

questions.stem: An insulator is a material with __________.
questions.explanation:
An insulator is a material that has tightly held electrons and very few, if any, free electrons. This
means that it can be used to protect the conductor since the insulator will not allow free
electrons from the conductor to knock lose any tightly held electrons of the insulator material.

questions.stem: Opposition to current flow is measured in __________.
questions.explanation:
The unit of measure for resistance or opposition to current flow is the ohm. It was agreed on
many years ago and has aided in making the electrical field progress so rapidly.

questions.stem: A watt is the power that gives rise to the production of energy at the rate of __________.
questions.explanation:
The watt is the unit of power in electrical work. It is defined as the production of energy at the
rate of one joule per second (per second is the basis for all electrical work).

questions.stem: The Greek letter phi () is used to __________.
questions.explanation:
The Greek alphabet is used almost in its entirety in the electrical field to represent various
quantities and effects. The Greek letter phi () is familiar if you have been looking at three-phase
power. It is used to represent the phases of electrical power.

questions.stem:
A parallel circuit with resistors of 10 ohms, 10 ohms, and 5 ohms has a total resistance of
__________.
questions.explanation:
Total resistance of a parallel circuit can be found two ways: by using the reciprocal formula or by
using the product of two resistors divided by the sum of the two resistors divided by the sum of
the two and then using it again to obtain the final answer in the case of three in parallel. In this
case the two 10-ohm resistors will reduce to an equivalent of 5 ohms. This leaves, then, two 5-
ohm resistors in parallel, which reduce to 2.5 or half of the value of one.

questions.stem:
Which of these is a symbol for a fuse?

A.




B.

C.

D.
questions.explanation:
The symbols shown are for the resistor, the fuse, and the capacitor, as well as for a lamp or light
bulb. The one for the fuse is shown as in B.

questions.stem: How much voltage has a typical home outlet?
questions.explanation: A typical residential electrical outlet has 120 volts.

questions.stem:
A circuit contains three parallel resistors. Each resistor has 3 amps flowing through them.
What is the total current flowing through the circuit?
questions.explanation:
For resistors in parallel, the total current is equal to the sum of the currents through each
resistor.

questions.stem: A capacitor of 100 micro farads has a capacity of __________.
questions.explanation:
A microfarad is 1 million picofarads. Therefore, if you wish to convert micro farads to picofarads,
you have to multiply by 1 million. That means the answer is "100,000,000 picofarads" because
100 times 1 million is 100 million.

questions.stem: Impedance is represented by the symbol __________.
questions.explanation: Impedance is the total opposition to current flow in a circuit. It has its own symbol, Z.

questions.stem: In electronics this symbol represents a __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol shown represents a diode.

questions.stem: A junction diode is used for __________.

options.A: rectifying power-line frequencies and lower currents.
options.B: rectifying power-line frequencies and higher currents.
options.C: rectifying higher frequencies at lower currents.
options.D: rectifying higher frequencies at higher currents.

questions.explanation:
A junction diode has a larger surface area than a point-contact diode, therefore it can be used to
handle larger currents at power-line frequencies.

questions.stem: The SCR is a __________.
questions.explanation:
The SCR is a special type of rectifier. It is used in control circuits. The name SCR was a
descriptive one given it by General Electric Company engineers and it caught on in the
literature. Its correct name is not silicon- controlled rectifier but thyristor.

questions.stem: In an FM receiver the AFC is __________.

options.A: automatic frequency control for stabilizing the IF.
options.B: automatic frequency control for stabilizing the local oscillator.
options.C: automatic frequency control for tuning the incoming frequency.
options.D: automatic frequency control for the radio frequency amplifier.

questions.explanation:
On an FM receiver the AFC is automatic frequency control. It keeps the receiver from drifting
from the station it is tuned to. This is done by having part of the signal fed back to the local
oscillator to keep it operating on the correct frequency and not drifting.

questions.stem: The symbol above represents a __________.
questions.explanation: The symbol shown represents a resistor.

questions.stem: The FM band covers __________.
questions.explanation: The FM band covers 88 to 108 MHz. The AM band covers 550 to 1600 kilohertz.

questions.stem: The two most commonly used metals in solder are __________.
questions.explanation: Typical solders are almost equal parts tin and lead.

questions.stem: A properly soldered connection will appear __________.
questions.explanation: Shiny joints indicate a properly soldered connection.

questions.stem: Which electronic component can store charge?
questions.explanation:
A capacitor can store a charge. A capacitor stores energy in an electric field. Positive charges
collect on one
plate and negative charges on the other plate.

questions.stem: Most wires are made from __________.
questions.explanation: Copper has a high conductivity and is financially cheaper than most metals.

questions.stem:
Most 12V car battery are made up of six individual cells connected in series.
What is the voltage of each cell in a car battery?
questions.explanation:
Voltages in series are added to determine the total voltage, so divide 12 volts by 6 cells to get 2
volts. To be exact, each cell in a car battery provides 2.1 volts for a total of 12.6 volts when
connected in a series and at full charge.

questions.stem: What is the frequency of the alternating voltage and current typically used in the United States?
questions.explanation: Electricity in the U.S. has a frequency of 60hz.

questions.stem: What should the temperature of a typical soldering iron be when joining two wires together?
questions.explanation:
To properly melt solder, you should use a soldering iron heated between 500 and 600 degrees
Fahrenheit.

questions.stem:
What is the voltage across the load R and the current through R when the switch is open in the
following circuit?

options.A: The current is 0A; the voltage is 10V.
options.B: The current is 2A; the voltage is 10V.
options.C: The current is 2A; the voltage is 2V.
options.D: The current is 0A; the voltage is 0V.

questions.explanation: When the switch is open, no current flows. The voltage VR is I times R, which equals 0(5) = 0.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT needed to produce electrical power from fossil fuels?
questions.explanation: Dams are used to produce power from water.

questions.stem:
An AA battery produces a potential difference of 1.5V. Four AA batteries are placed in series to
power a portable FM radio.
What is the total voltage of the radio?
questions.explanation:
Voltages in series are added to determine the total voltage.
1.5V + 1.5V + 1.5V + 1.5V = 6.0V.

questions.stem:
Two 8-ohm speakers are connected in parallel to an amplifier with a 24-volt output.
What is the voltage across each speaker?
questions.explanation: Resistances in parallel have the same voltage across them.

questions.stem: Which function does the receiving antenna provide in radio communication?

options.A: It catches the signal out of the air.
options.B: It separates the carrier wave from the signal.
options.C: It mixes the signal and the carrier wave.
options.D: It broadcasts the signal over the air.

questions.explanation:
The broadcast antenna is used to broadcast the signal over the air. The mixer combines the
signal and carrier wave. The de-mixer separates the carrier and the signal.

questions.stem:
A current meter is connected to a circuit as shown.
What does the current meter read?
questions.explanation:
The current through the meter is equal to the current through R1. The current through R1 is 45V
/ 10 = 4.5A

questions.stem: An oscilloscope is typically used to analyze __________.
questions.explanation: An oscilloscope is used primarily to look at complex waveforms.

questions.stem: Printed circuit boards are typically made out of __________.
questions.explanation: Fiberglass is used to make most printed circuit boards.

When an electric current passes through a wire, a __________ field is generated around the

A 120V light bulb is rated for 40 watts.
What is the light bulb's current rating?
questions.explanation: P = IV, so I = P/V or I = 40 Watts/120V = 1/3A

questions.stem: What color is Neutral wire?
questions.explanation: Neutral wire is whitish (or natural) colored.

questions.stem: What voltage will cause an 8 Amp current to flow through a 24 ohm resistor?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law is V = IR, so V = 8 × 24 = 192 volts

questions.explanation: The symbol is a standard representation of an inductor.

questions.explanation: AC is an abbreviation for Alternating Current.

Two 16 ohm speakers are connected in parallel to an amplifier that provides a 32 volt output.

Use Ohm's law - V=IR. The total resistance in the circuit is 10 ohms (add the resistance for
serial resistors).

questions.stem: What is the reading on the kilowatt-hour meter shown below?
questions.explanation:
The meter has four dials with the numbers 0 to 9. The pointers rotate in different directions.
Read the dials from the left, using the number the dial pointer just passed.

questions.explanation: The symbol is a standard representation of a diode.

questions.stem: What is the voltage across and current through the resistor R when the switch is open?
questions.explanation: When the switch is open, there is no voltage or current.

questions.explanation:
The meter has four dials with the numbers 0 to 9. The pointers rotate in different directions.
Read the dials from the left, using the number the dial pointer just passed.

questions.stem: Resistance is measured in __________.
questions.explanation: Resistance is measure in ohms.

questions.stem: What is the total resistance when two 10 ohm resistors are connected in series?
questions.explanation:
When resistors are in series, you simply add their resistance together to find a total resistance.
10 + 10 = 20 ohms.

questions.stem: Using a fuse rated higher than the required current rating of a circuit can __________.

options.B: cause the fuse to blow more often
options.C: lower your power usage for that circuit
options.D: result in serious damage to your circuit

questions.explanation:
Using a higher rated fuse is dangerous and can result in serious damage to your circuit.

questions.stem: What are the major layers of Earth's atmosphere in order from the Earth's surface upward?

options.A: Troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, exo sphere
options.C: Troposphere, tropopause, ionosphere, stratosphere, exo sphere

questions.explanation:
The five major layers of the atmosphere from the Earth's surface upward are the troposphere,
stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere, and exosphere.
The troposphere starts at the Earth's surface and extends to between 23,000 ft (7 km) at the
poles and 60,000 ft (17 km) at the equator, with some variations due to weather factors.
The stratosphere extends from the top of the troposphere (23,000-60,000 ft or 7-17 km) to about
160,000 ft (60 km).
The stratosphere contains the ozone layer, which is mainly located in the lower part of the
stratosphere from about 50,000-115,000 ft (15-35 km) above the surface, although the
thickness varies somewhat across both the seasons and the Earth's geographical regions.
The mesosphere extends from about 160,000 ft (50 km) to about 265,000-285,000 ft (50-54
miles or 80-85 km).
This is also where most meteors bum up when entering the atmosphere

is the study of past human life and culture by the recovery or discovery and examination of

same atomic number (i.e., the same number of protons) but a different number of neutrons.

questions.stem: Antibodies __________.

options.A: identify and neutralize foreign objects inside the body.
options.B: bond with antigens to keep the body's hormones balanced.
options.C: prevent infection by blocking access to the circulatory system.
options.D: are produced by the endocrine system.

questions.explanation:
Antibodies identify and neutralize foreign objects inside the body. Humans and other vertebrates
have an immune system that uses antibodies to fight bacteria, viruses, toxins, and other foreign
objects. Antibodies are complex, Y-shaped protein molecules that develop from plasma cells,
which in turn develop from "B lymphocytes" produced by the bone marrow. The plasma cells
can generate a very large array of different antibodies, each of which can combine with and
destroy an antigen (foreign molecule).
Antibodies react to very specific characteristics of different antigens, binding them to the top
ends of their Y- shaped form. Once the antibody and antigen combine, the antibodies deactivate
the antigen or lead it to macrophages (a type of white blood cell) that ingest and destroy it.
High counts of a particular antibody may persist for months after an invasion before eventually
diminishing.
However, the B cells can quickly manufacture more of the same antibody if exposure to that
particular antigen reoccurs.
Vaccines work by "training" B cells to recognize and react quickly to potential disease
molecules.

expression at a time. What gives you x2? The answer is x times x. Therefore, place an x at the
beginning of each factor.
(x)(x)
Next find the two numbers you would multiply to get 10. The numbers could be 10 and 1, or 5
and 2, but
remember that the two numbers also have to produce 3, the middle term in the polynomial. The
difference between 5 and 2 is 3. Therefore 5 and 2 are the numbers that complete the factors (x
- 5)(x + 2)
Now decide the signs that belong in each factor. The appearance of -10 in the polynomial
means that 5 and 2 have different signs. The -3x in the polynomial indicates that 5 (the larger
number) has the minus sign, and that 2 has a plus sign. Thus
(x - 5)(x + 2)
Step 3: Set each factor equal to zero and solve the equations.
x - 5 = 0x + 2 = 0
x = 5
x = -2

This problem does not have to be computed, because the two symbols cancel each other. The
radical sign () in (13) tells you to find the square root of 13. But the exponent (2) tells you to
square the answer - that is, to multiply the square root of 13 by itself. This would get you back to
13.

questions.stem:
Mr. Langendorfer drove his car steadily at 40 miles per hour for 120 miles. He then increased
his speed and drove the next 120 miles at 60 miles per hour.
What was his average speed?
questions.explanation:
To find the average rate of speed (mph), divide the distance he covered by the time he spent
traveling (R = D/ T). In this example, begin by finding the distance traveled.
120 + 120 = 240 miles (distance)
Next find the length of time he traveled.
At the beginning of his trip, he drove 120 miles at 40 mph.
120 / 40 = 3 hours (first part of trip)
Later, he increased his speed.
120 / 60 = 2 hours (second part of trip)
Altogether, he traveled for 5 hours. Now apply the formula for finding his average rate of speed
D/T = 240/5 = 48 mph (rate of speed)

questions.stem:
An architect designs two walls of a museum to meet at an angle of 120 degrees.
What is an angle of this size called?
questions.explanation:
An angle of 180 degrees is a straight angle. An angle of 90 degrees is a right angle. An angle
greater than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees is an obtuse angle. An angle less than 90
degrees is an acute angle.

questions.stem:
Solve the following equations for x.
5x + 4y = 27
x - 2y=11
questions.explanation:
To solve these equations for x, begin by finding a way to eliminate y.
Multiply both sides of the second equation by 2.
2(x - 2y) = 2 × 11
2x - 4y = 22
Add the new form of the second equation to the first equation, and solve for x.
5x + 4y = 27
2x - 4y = 22
(+4 cancels -4)
7x = 49
x = 7

questions.stem: If a is a negative number, and ab is a positive number, then which of the following must be true?
questions.explanation:
The product of a negative number and a positive number is always negative. The product of two



negative numbers is always a positive number. Since ab is positive and a is negative, b must be
negative, too.

questions.stem:
Solve the following inequality.
x + 5 > 7
questions.explanation:
The expression (x + 5 > 7) is a statement of inequality, it means that x plus 5 is greater than 7 -
not equal to it.
To solve this inequality, subtract 5 from both sides of the statement.
x + 5 > 7
x + 5 - 5 > 7 - 5
x > 2
Thus the statement of inequality is true for any value of x that is greater than 2. Try it with 3, for
example.
3 + 5 > 7
8 > 7 a true statement

combined, but the two final zeros may be dropped since they are to the right of the decimal
point and at the end.

questions.stem: If 2x - 3 = 37, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation:
The equation 2x - 3 = 37 means that "twice a number minus 3 is equal to 37." To arrive at a
value for x, we first eliminate -3 on the left side. This can be done by adding 3 to both sides of
the equation, thus undoing the subtraction.
2x - 3 + 3 = 37 + 3
2x = 40
To eliminate the 2 that multiplies x, we undo the multiplication by dividing both sides of the
equation by 2.
2x/2 = 40/2 = 20

questions.stem:
For a special operations air assault mission, one extra soldier for the security element is to be
chosen at
random from among three soldiers from the 327th Infantry Regiment, two soldiers from the
502nd Infantry Regiment, and five soldiers from the 187th Infantry Regiment.
What is the probability that a soldier from the 327th Infantry Regiment will be chosen?
questions.explanation:
The probability of an event occurring is the number of "favorable'' outcomes divided by the total
possible number of outcomes.
Since there are three soldiers from the 327th from which to choose, there are three possible
favorable outcomes for choosing a soldier from that unit.
Since the choice will be made from among a total of 10 soldiers, there are 10 different possible
outcomes.
The probability of choosing a soldier from the 327th Infantry Regiment is 3/10.

A cylindrical post has a cross section that is a circle with a radius of 3 inches. A piece of cord
can be wound around it exactly seven times.
How long is the piece of cord? Use 22/7 as the value of .
questions.explanation:
A length of cord that will wind around once is equal to the circumference of the circle whose
radius is 3 inches.
The circumference of a circle equals 2% r where n =22:7 and r is the radius.
Circumference = 22/1 × 22/7 × 3/1 =132/7 inches
If the cord can be wound around the post seven times, its length is seven times the length of
one circumference.
Length of cord 132/7 × 7/1 = 132 inches

questions.stem:
A naval task force is to be made up of a destroyer, a supply ship, and a submarine.
If four destroyers, two supply ships, and three submarines are available from which to choose,
how many different combinations are possible for the task force?
questions.explanation:
There are four possible choices for the destroyer.
Each of these choices may be coupled with any of the two choices for the supply ship.
Each such destroyer-supply ship combination may in rum be coupled with any of the three
possible choices for the submarine.
Thus, there are 4 × 2 × 3, or 24, different combinations possible.

questions.stem:
The base of a cylindrical can is a circle whose diameter is 2 inches. Its height is 7 inches.
How many cubic inches are there in the volume of the can? Use 22/7 for the value of .
questions.explanation:
The volume of a cylinder is equal to the product of its height and the area of its base. The base
is a circle. The area of a circle is r2, where  = 22/7 and r is the radius. Since the diameter is 2
inches, the radius (which is one-half the diameter) is 1 inch.
Area of circular base =
22/7 × 1/1 × 1/1 = 22/7
The height is 7 inches.
22/7 × 7/1 = 22 cubic inches

questions.stem:
A rectangular vegetable garden 16 yards long and 4 yards wide is completely enclosed by a
fence. To reduce the amount of fencing used, the owner replaced the garden with a square one
having the same area.
How many yards of fencing did he save?
questions.explanation:
The area of the rectangular garden is equal to the product of its length and width. Area of
rectangle = 16 × 4 = 64 square yards.
In order for the square to have the same area, 64 square yards, its sides must each be 8 yards
long, since 8 × 8 = 64 square yards. The fence around the rectangular garden has a length of
16 + 4 + 16 + 4, or 40, yards.
The fence around the square garden has a length of 4 × 8, or 32, yards.
The saving in fencing is 40 - 32, or 8, yards.

What is the maximum number of boxes, each measuring 3 inches by 4 inches by 5 inches, that

inches as 12 inches by 24 inches by 25 inches. Boxes measuring 3 inches by 4 inches by 5
inches can be stacked so that four of the 3-inch sides make up the 12-inch storage dimension,
six of the 4-inch sides fill the 24-inch storage dimension, and five of the 5-inch sides fill the 25-
inch storage dimension.
There will be 4 × 6 × 5, or 120, boxes packed into the storage space.

A circle passes through the four vertices of a rectangle that is 8 feet long and 6 feet wide.
How many feet are there in the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation:
If the circle passes through all four vertices of the rectangle, its diameter will be a diagonal of
the rectangle.
Since a rectangle's angles are right angles, the diagonal for n is a right triangle with two sides of
the rectangle.
Let x = the length of the diagonal. By the Pythagorean Theorem, in a right triangle the square of
the length of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of the legs.
x2 = 82 + 62
x2 = 64 + 36
x2 = 100
x2 = 100
means that x times x=100.
Therefore, x = 10 feet.
But 10 is a diameter of the circle. A radius of a circle is one-half the diameter. Hence, the radius
is 5 feet.

Use the FOIL method (First, Outside, Inside, Last) to solve.

In privatization, the government relies on the private sector to provide a service. However, the
government divests itself of the entire process, including all assets. With privatized functions,
the government may specify quality, quantity, and timeliness requirements, but it has no control
over the operations of the activity. Also, the government may not be the only customer.
Whoever the government chooses to provide the services would likely provide the same
services to others.
This paragraph best supports the statement that __________.

options.A: the government must closely supervise privatized functions
options.B: privatized functions consist of a mixture of government employees, military personnel, and private contractors
options.C: privatized functions are those institutions that provide services only to a government agency
options.D: privatized functions provide essential services to the government

questions.explanation:
Privatized functions operate independently of the government, making Choices "the government
must closely supervise privatized functions" and "privatized functions consist of a mixture of
government employees, military personnel, and private contractors" incorrect.
The passage states that privatized functions may sell goods and services to other customers as
well as the government, so Choice "privatized functions are those institutions that provide
services only to a government agency" is also incorrect.
Choice "privatized functions provide essential services to the government" is the correct answer,
as privatized functions do perform essential services to government agencies.

Many criminal-law statutes permit more severe punishment of a person convicted of a crime if
he or she intended to harm another person. For example, voluntary manslaughter carries a
heavier penalty than involuntary manslaughter in most states. Planned crimes are also punished
more severely than spur-of-the- moment crimes. The problem is that juries find it difficult to
know what the intent of a person was at the time he or she committed a crime. Many defendants

"accidental." The law asks too much of juries when it expects them to determine what a person
was thinking. Juries should only be asked to weigh objective evidence.

In the military, as in all professions, the issue of competence is directly relevant to professional
integrity. Because human life, national security, and expenditures from the national treasury are
so frequently at issue when the military acts, the obligation to be competent isn't merely
prudential. That obligation is a moral one, and culpable incompetence here is clearly a violation
of professional integrity. Part of the social aspect of professional integrity involves the joint
responsibility for conduct and competence shared by all members of the profession. Only fellow
professionals are capable of evaluating competence in some instances; hence, fellow
professionals must accept the responsibility of upholding the standards of the profession. Fellow
military members can spot derelictions of duty, failures of leadership, failures of competence,
and the venalities of conduct that interfere with the goals of the military mission. Often, the
obligations of professional integrity may be pitted against personal loyalties or friendships; and,
where the stakes for society are so high, professional integrity should win out.

passage.

except the 1848 Mexican War. However, they were almost always restricted to segregated,
black-only units - usually with white officers - until after the Korean War. President Harry S.
Truman issued an executive order in 1948 that mandated "equality of treatment... in the armed
services without regard to race, color, religion or national origin." By October 1953, the Army



announced that 95 percent of black soldiers were serving in integrated units.
By when was segregation of black soldiers effectively ended?
questions.explanation:
Even though President Truman ordered an end to segregation in 1948, it was not effectively
ended until 1953, by which time the Army announced that 95 percent of black soldiers were
serving in integrated units.

split it with you, but says that, in order to show your "good faith," you have to put up some of
your own money. When you agree to give him your money, the stranger finds a reason to leave
for a while. Do you see him again? Probably not - you have just been conned.
The main theme of this passage is __________.

options.C: how to make lots of money
options.D: don't believe anything a stranger says

This passage warns the reader of one particular get-rich-quick scheme, and by extension
cautions them to be wary of all such ideas.

stranger says - if we did that, we couldn't go in a convenience store on a long trip to buy gas or
go to the restroom.
The passage also does not describe how to make lots of money, since the subject of the con
loses money rather than getting rich.
