LLC stands for "Limited Liability Corporation," meaning the business owners' liability is limited.
Without the idea of "limited liability," the owners of a business can be held personally
responsible for the debts of their business. The idea of "limited liability" originated in Germany in
the late 19th century. By the 1940s, the idea had taken hold in 17 countries, but not the United
States. In 1977, Wyoming became the first U.S. state to pass an LLC law modeled after the
German statute. Many other states eventually passed their own version, though most of them
have variations from other states.
Why is the idea of limited liability helpful to business owners?

options.A: Because it can limit their personal financial risk.
options.B: Because it is a tradition dating back to the 19th century.
options.C: Because it is now legal in all 50 states.
options.D: Because it holds them personally responsible for their business' debts.

questions.explanation:
The idea of a limited liability company or LLC is helpful to business owners because it can limit
the financial risk to them personally, rather than making business owners personally responsible
for the debts of their business.
This idea is expressed in the first two sentences of the passage; it is left for the reader to
understand that decreased personal financial risk is better, but that's a conclusion most people
would easily reach on their own.

more capable whole. It is the strengthened unity resulting from diversity that is important, not
just diversity for its own sake.

organization or group. The writer of this passage is trying to get across the idea that the
advantage of diversity is the increased strength and capability that the diverse group has over

why is it important? Ozone is an invisible gas. There is a thin layer of it about 15 miles above
the surface of the Earth. Some of the sun's rays can be harmful to us and ozone helps protect
us from damage. Unfortunately, the amount of ozone in our atmosphere has been reduced in
the past few years and scientists think they know how this happened. Humans have produced
chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which have caused a decrease in ozone. One other effect of
reduced ozone involves climate change. If more of the sun's rays reach the Earth, they can
cause changing weather patterns and a warmer climate. Possible disastrous effects of this
change include the increased incidence of tornadoes and droughts.

About 2 to 3 out of every 1,000 children in the United States are born deaf or hard of hearing.
Over 90% of these children are born to parents who can hear. Early identification of children
who are born deaf or hard of hearing is critical to ensure that their families have the resources
they need to help their children acquire language, spoken and/or visual, and achieve age-
appropriate communicative, cognitive, academic, social, and emotional development. The
National Association for the Deaf (NAD) supported passage of the Early Hearing Detection and
Intervention Act (EHDI) in 2000 and subsequent federal funding to establish state newborn
hearing screening programs in hospitals. At the time, the average age of identification of deaf
children was about 21/2 years old; children who were hard of hearing were often identified much
later. The goals of the EHDI program include hearing screening of all newborns by age one
month, confirmation of hearing status by three months, and enrollment in an early intervention
program for deaf and hard of hearing babies and their families by six months.

questions.passage:
About 2 to 3 out of every 1,000 children in the United States are born deaf or hard of hearing.
Over 90% of these children are born to parents who can hear. Early identification of children
who are born deaf or hard of hearing is critical to ensure that their families have the resources
they need to help their children acquire language, spoken and/or visual, and achieve age-
appropriate communicative, cognitive, academic, social, and emotional development. The
National Association for the Deaf (NAD) supported passage of the Early Hearing Detection and
Intervention Act (EHDI) in 2000 and subsequent federal funding to establish state newborn
hearing screening programs in hospitals. At the time, the average age of identification of deaf
children was about 21/2 years old; children who were hard of hearing were often identified much
later. The goals of the EHDI program include hearing screening of all newborns by age one
month, confirmation of hearing status by three months, and enrollment in an early intervention
program for deaf and hard of hearing babies and their families by six months.

questions.stem:
In the figure above, if Gear 1 has 25 teeth and Gear 2 has 15 teeth, how many revolutions does

questions.explanation:

revolutions it makes (R).
Divide that number by the number of teeth Gear 2 has D to determine the number of revolutions
Gear 2 makes (r).
Because the gears are proportional, this formula will show you the ratio of teeth to revolutions.
r = DR/d
r = (25 × 10)/15

questions.stem:
A cubic foot of water weighs about 62.5 pounds.
If an aquarium is 18 feet long, 10 feet deep, and 12 feet wide, what's the approximate pounds-
per-square-inch pressure (psi) on the bottom of the tank?
questions.explanation:
You can determine the pressure of all that water by multiplying the volume of the aquarium by
the weight of the water. Volume = lwh.
The bottom of the tank is 18 feet long by 12 feet wide by 10 feet high for a total volume of 2,160
cubic feet (18 × 12 × 10).
A cubic foot of water weighs approximately 62.5 pounds.
2,160 × 62.5 gives an approximate pressure on the bottom of the tank of about 135,000 pounds
over the entire surface area.
The surface area of the bottom of the tank is length × width.
216 inches (18 feet × 12) × 144 inches (12 feet × 12) = 31,104.
Dividing the pressure of 135,000 by the number of square inches of surface area gives an
approximate PSI of 4.

Gear 1 makes 10 clockwise revolutions per minute.
Gear 2, which is half the size, makes 20 counterclockwise revolutions per minute. (The number
of revolutions it makes is inversely proportional to its difference in size.)
Gear 2 is half the size of Gear 1, so to determine the number of revolutions it makes, multiply
the number of revolutions Gear 1 makes by the inverse of 1/2: 10 × 2/1 (or just 2) = 20.
Gear 3 is 2.5 times the size of Gear 2. In other words, it is 5/2 the size of Gear 2.
To determine the number of revolutions Gear 3 makes, multiply the inverse of 5/2 by the
number of revolutions Gear 2 makes: 2/5 × 20.
This can be stated as 20/1 (the number of revolutions Gear 2 makes per minute) × 2/5 (the
fraction of revolutions Gear 3 makes) = 40/5 or 8 revolutions per minute.

The figure above represents a water tank.
Which of the following statements is not true?

options.A: If Valves 1 and 2 are open and Valves 3, 4, and 5 are closed, the tank will eventually overflow.
options.B: If all valves are open, the water remains at a constant level as long as the rate of intake is equal to the rate of discharge.
options.C: Water in the tank will rise if Valves 1 and 2 are open and Valves 3 and 4 are closed.
options.D: The tank will empty entirely if Valves 1 and 2 are closed and Valves 4 and 5 are open.

questions.explanation:
Because Valve 4 is above the bottom of the tank, some water will remain in the tank below the
level of the valve, so the tank will never be completely empty.

questions.stem: Heat is a form of ___________.
questions.explanation:
Heat is a form of energy - Calories measure heat, beneficence is an attitude or emotion, and
motion is something that can cause heat.

questions.stem: The lift caused by an aircraft's wings is primarily due to ___________.

options.A: a decrease in pressure on the upper side of the wing (A)
options.B: a decrease in pressure on the bottom side of the wing B
options.C: a vacuum created under the wing at point B
options.D: an increase in pressure on the upper side of the wing (A)

questions.explanation:
When oncoming air meets the leading edge of the airfoil (wing), some of it goes over the top of



the airfoil and some of it flows underneath.
The air flowing over the top of the wing has to go further than the air underneath, because it
must join together again with the air that flowed under the wing at the far (back) side of the wing
- physical laws act together to prevent or minimize vacuums in most cases.

questions.stem: Pliers are an example of a ___________.
questions.explanation:
Pliers are an example of a first-class lever because the fulcrum is positioned between the effort
(where your hand grips the pliers) and the load (the object that is being held or squeezed by the
pliers).

questions.stem:
The wheels below are connected by a belt as shown.
If the larger wheel makes two revolutions, how many revolutions will the smaller wheel make?
questions.explanation:
We are not told the sizes of the two wheels, but we can see that one is larger than the other.
If the two wheels are connected by a belt, the small wheel will be forced to turn fester and
complete more turns than the larger wheel.

questions.stem: If the wheel on the left turns clockwise, which way will the wheel on the right turn?

options.D: Unable to tell from the information given

questions.explanation: If the wheel on the left turns clockwise, the wheel on the right will turn counterclockwise.

questions.stem:
How can a gear system derive the greatest amount of mechanical advantage when a seven-
tooth gear drives a ___________?
questions.explanation:
The greater the difference between the number of teeth of the two meshed gears, the greater
the torque or mechanical advantage.

questions.stem:
An above-ground suburban water tank holds 540 gallons of water when full.
If the tank starts out full and is drained at a rate of 60 gallons per minute, how many seconds
will it take to empty out halfway?
questions.explanation:
540 gallons divided by 60 gallons a minute means that it takes nine minutes to drain the tank
completely.
Half of that time is 4.5 minutes; 4.5 multiplied by 60 seconds equals 270 seconds.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a simple machine?
questions.explanation:
An axe is a compound machine: the handle is a lever, and the head is two inclined planes (each
side of the blade edge).

questions.stem:
If you want to hammer in a heavy nail, it might be a good idea to use a hammer with a
__________.
questions.explanation:
A longer handle - a longer lever - allows the hammerhead to reach a higher speed, thereby
producing more striking force.

questions.stem:
If you drag a log across the road, one way to reduce the amount of force needed to pull it would
be to ___________.
questions.explanation:
If you drag a log across the road, one way to reduce the amount of force needed to pull it would
be to lubricate the road.
Two things contribute to the force needed to pull the log across the road: the weight (mass) of
the log itself, and the friction between the log and the road.
Lubricating the road will reduce the friction and therefore reduce the force needed to pull the log
across the road.

questions.stem:
Presume that Pulley C is rotating clockwise.
What direction will Pulley A rotate?
questions.explanation:
By rotating clockwise. Pulley C will cause Pulley B to rotate counterclockwise, which will in turn
cause Pulley A to rotate clockwise.

questions.stem: The rate at which work is done is called __________.
questions.explanation:
The English unit of power is foot pound per second. It takes 550 foot pounds to make 1
horsepower. The SI unit is the joule per second or watt. A horsepower is 746 watts. The rate at
which work is done is called power.
Power is work done per unit of time.

questions.stem: Forces existing in pairs are sometimes called __________.
questions.explanation:
A force cannot be exerted unless there is something there to push back. Forces exist in pairs.
For every action there is a reaction.

questions.stem: When forces act in pairs they are ___________.

options.A: equal in magnitude and opposite in direction
options.B: equal in magnitude and in the same direction

questions.explanation:
Since it is impossible to have one force unless it acts as one of a pair of forces, it means that
these forces must be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

questions.stem: Which pendulum takes less time to make one complete back-and-forth swing?

options.C: Both take the same amount of time.
options.D: There is not enough information to calculate the answer.

questions.explanation:
The length of time it takes for one all back and forth swing depends on the length of the string,
not the weight at the end of it.

questions.stem:
When you heat water that is confined in a closed container so that the steam cannot escape,
the pressure inside the container __________ and the temperature of the boiling water
__________.
questions.explanation:
Heating an enclosed container of boiling water increases the pressure of the water vapor
(steam) inside the



container and increases the temperature of the water.

questions.stem: If Block A, on which the lever is resting, is moved farther away from Block B __________.

options.A: it will be harder to lift Block B but it will go higher
options.B: it will be easier to lift Block B and it will go higher
options.C: it will be harder to lift Block B and it will not be lifted to the same height
options.D: it will be easier to lift Block B but it will not be lifted as high

questions.explanation:
It will be harder to lift Block B but it will go higher.
If Block A under the beam serving as the lever is moved away from Block B on top of the lever
beam, the moment for the force exerted will increase, since the fulcrum is now closer to the
force; this will make Block B harder to lift.
However, the height to which Block B on the end of the lever beam can be raised increases the
further away Block A is moved from Block B.

questions.stem: For two gears to mesh properly, they must __________.

options.D: have the same number of teeth

questions.explanation:
For two gears to mesh properly, they must have the same size teeth.
Different size gears will, by definition, rotate at different speeds even when their driving axles
are moving at the same speed.
Also, interlocking or meshing gears rotate in opposite directions.

questions.stem: Kinetic energy is __________.

options.A: energy stored in chemicals, such as in a battery.
options.B: energy in moving electrons, as in an electric current.
options.D: energy that can be released under certain conditions.

questions.explanation:
Kinetic energy is energy in a moving object.
Energy stored in chemicals, such as in a battery, is chemical energy; energy in moving
electrons, as in an electric current, is electric energy; and energy that can be released under
certain conditions is potential energy.

questions.stem:
The amount that a machine (simple or complex) multiplies your force or effort is called
__________.
questions.explanation:
The amount that a machine (simple or complex) multiplies your force or effort is called
mechanical advantage.
Load distance is how far the load moves when force is applied, and acceleration is the change
in velocity or speed in a certain direction.

questions.stem: The mechanical advantage of two meshing gears is calculated by dividing __________.

options.A: the number of teeth on the driving gear by the number of teeth on the driven gear.
options.B: the number of teeth on the driven gear by the number of teeth on the driving gear.
options.C: the number of teeth on the driving gear by the rotational speed.
options.D: the diameter of the driven gear by the number of teeth on the driving gear.

questions.explanation:
The mechanical advantage of two meshing gears is calculated by dividing the number of teeth
on the driven gear by the number of teeth on the driving gear.

questions.stem: A compound machine is one in which __________.

options.B: one simple machine rotates around the second one
options.C: two or more simple machines work together
options.D: the mechanical advantages can be made to balance each other out

questions.explanation: A compound machine is one in which two or more simple machines work together.

questions.stem: When meshing or interlocking gears have different numbers of teeth, __________.

options.A: relative speeds depend on the speed of the drive aide for both
options.B: both gears will rotate at the same speed
options.C: the gear with more teeth will rotate fester than the gear with fewer teeth
options.D: the gear with fewer teeth will rotate fester than the gear with more teeth

questions.explanation:
When meshing or interlocking gears have different numbers of teeth, the gear with fewer teeth
will rotate faster than the gear with more teeth.
If two gears are meshed, both cannot be driven or something will break - one must be driving
and one must be driven.

questions.stem: Cranks are used to __________.

options.A: convert motion in a circle into motion in a straight line
options.B: convert motion in a straight line into motion in a circle
options.C: attach to rotating shafts to push separate pieces in a given direction
options.D: transfer power between rotating shafts of different diameters

questions.explanation:
Cranks are used to convert motion in a straight line into motion in a circle, such as in a bicycle's
pedals and pistons in an automotive engine.

questions.stem: Which of the other gears is moving in the opposite direction from Gear 1?
questions.explanation:
Meshed gears turn in opposite directions.
Gear 1 is turning clockwise; therefore.
Gear 2 is turning counterclockwise (the opposite direction from Gear 1) and Gear 3 is turning
clockwise (the same direction as Gear l).

questions.stem: Force is something that can change the velocity of an object by making it __________.
questions.explanation:
Force is something that can change the velocity of an object by making it start or stop, speed
up, or slow down.
This means that all the answers given are correct.

questions.stem:
The brakes on your car use the same force that stops your car if you just let it coast.
This force is called ___________.
questions.explanation:
Friction is used to stop a car.
The brakes rub against the wheel drum or the disc to cause the car to stop.
This rubbing is creating friction.

questions.stem:
As the central shaft in the illustration below spins faster in a clockwise direction, the balls
labeled A and B will ___________.
questions.explanation:
Centrifugal force from the spinning shaft, regardless of direction, will cause the balls to move
outward, away from the shaft; the tension on the strings holding them will result in the balls
moving upward.

questions.stem: If you drop something, the force acting on it is ____________.
questions.explanation:
Gravity is the force that pulls things down whenever they are dropped.
It is said that Isaac Newton "discovered" the concept of gravity as an identifiable force while
sitting under an apple tree and the obvious happened.
Gravity is created by the mass of the earth.
The pull of gravity is much less (about one-sixth) on the moon than on earth.

questions.stem:
In the illustration below, if Pulley A is rotating in the direction indicated, then Pulley C will
__________.

options.A: rotate in the same direction as Pulley B
options.B: rotate in the same direction as Pulleys A and B
options.C: rotate in the opposite direction of Pulleys A and B
options.D: rotate in the same direction as Pulley A

questions.explanation:
Pulley C will rotate in the same direction as Pulley A.
Pulley A causes Pulley B to rotate in the opposite direction from Pulley A, and Pulley B causes
Pulley C to rotate in the opposite direction from Pulley B.
Since there are only two directions of rotation available.
Pulley C's direction of rotation is the same as Pulley A.

questions.stem: In the pulley system shown, which pulley will rotate the fastest?

options.D: They will all rotate at the same speed.

questions.explanation:
Pulley B will rotate the fastest. Just like meshing gears, the smaller the pulley in a system, the
fester it rotates.

questions.stem: Weight is directly proportional to the acceleration due to ___________.
questions.explanation:
Weight is not a fixed property of an object; it varies with location.
Your weight is slightly less at the North Pole than it is at the equator.
Your weight is much less on the moon than on earth.
Everything weighs less where the acceleration due to gravity is smaller.
Weight is directly proportional to local acceleration due to gravity.

questions.stem:
The force that acts in an upward direction on anything submerged in a liquid or a gas is called
__________.
questions.explanation:
Buoyancy is the force that makes ships float and helium-filled balloons rise.
This means that the force that acts in an upward direction on anything submerged in a liquid or
a gas is called buoyancy.

questions.stem:
In the illustration below, two 30-lbs blocks are attached to the ceiling using ropes, as shown.
Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: All the ropes are under equal amounts of tension.
options.B: The rope supporting Block A is under 2x the tension of the ropes holding Block B.
options.C: The ropes supporting Block B are under 1/3 of the tension of the rope holding Block A.
options.D: The rope holding Block A is under 1/3 of the tension of the ropes holding Block B.

questions.explanation:
There are three ropes supporting Block B; therefore, they are under 1/3 the tension as the rope
supporting Block A.

questions.stem: When the plug in the tube is removed, water will flow ___________.
questions.explanation:
When the plug is removed, water will flow into the tube to equalize the water level both inside
and outside the tube.

questions.stem: If an object is in equilibrium, it is said to be __________.

options.C: at rest or moving at a constant speed and in a straight line

questions.explanation:
An object in equilibrium may or may not be at rest.



If two or more forces act, their effects may eliminate each other.
When this condition of equilibrium is reached, there is no net force and the velocity does not
change.
Equilibrium is reached when the object is at rest or moving at a constant speed and in a straight
line.

questions.stem: In the figure, the angle b is important, since when it is __________.

options.A: 0 degrees the entire force is dragging the box
options.B: 90 degrees the entire force is lifting the box
options.C: both lifting and dragging between 10 degrees and 90 degrees

questions.explanation:
The angle of the rope determines if the box is being pulled along the floor or being lifted from
the floor.
That means it can be both lifted and pulled along at any angle that is more than 0 degrees and
less than 90 degrees.

questions.stem: A good example of a simple machine is a __________.
questions.explanation:
Simple machines are devices that make work easier.
Some examples of simple machines are levers, hydraulic jacks, loading ramps, vises, and



machines that spin - winches and gears.
Door knobs, light switches, and manually operated pencil sharpeners are also simple machines.

questions.stem:
Which weight exerts more pull on the horizontal bar from which both weights hang by strings as
shown?

options.D: Insufficient information to solve this problem

questions.explanation:
The string holding the 10-lb. weight exerts more pull on the bar.
The fact that that string is longer does not change how much tension is on it due to the weight at
its end.

questions.stem:
In the water system shown below, assume that the main tank starts empty and that all the
valves are closed.
In order for the tank to fill about halfway and keep that level, which valves have to be open?
questions.explanation:
Valves A, B, and D must be open for the tank to fill halfway and maintain that level.
Water flows in through Valve A (meaning that any choice not including Valve A is automatically
incorrect), and flows out when the tank is half full through Valve B.
However, for that water to leave the system. Valve D must also be open.

questions.stem: Work input is always more than work output because of __________.
questions.explanation:
Efficiency is affected by friction. It is a ratio of how much effort went into a job compared to what
was produced or outputted.
Therefore, work input is more than the work output. Friction accounts for the loss in efficiency.

questions.stem: The ratio between work output and work input is called __________.
questions.explanation:
In order to find out how well work was performed and how much effort was expended in getting
the job done, the term efficiency is used to describe the ratio of work input to work output.

questions.stem: The amount of magnification that a machine produces is referred to as the __________.
questions.explanation:
By using a machine, it is possible to multiply the amount of effort expended to get a job done.
Mechanical advantage is the amount of magnification, or the ratio of load to effort.

questions.stem: A ramp is a device commonly used to aid in __________.
questions.explanation:
A ramp is a device commonly used to aid in lifting.
The ramp is an inclined plane.



The work output of an inclined plane is the work that would have to be done to lift the load
directly.
The work input is the actual force exerted in pushing the load up the ramp times the length of
the ramp.
An ideal mechanical advantage of an inclined plane is equal to its length divided by its height.

questions.stem: A screw consists of a single continuous spiral wrapped around a __________.
questions.explanation:
A screw is a simple device. It has been used for centuries as a means of lifting water out of
wells and over the banks of irrigation canals.
A screw consists of a single continuous spiral wrapped around a cylinder.
The threads are cut into a rod in a spiral and make it possible to use the holding power of the
screw in fastening objects together.

questions.stem: If Pulley A is the driver and turns counterclockwise, which pulley will turn the slowest?
questions.explanation: The pulley that is the largest will turn most slowly.

questions.stem:
The mechanical advantage of a winch is the ratio of the radius of the crank to the radius of the
__________.
questions.explanation:
The principle of a winch is not much different from that of a lever.
Since the crank and the shaft turn together, the torque exerted by the effort (the force on the
handle) must be equal to the torque exerted by the load (the tension in the rope).
The mechanical advantage then is the ratio of the radius of the crank to the radius of the shaft.

questions.stem:
The ideal mechanical advantage of a gear is the ratio of the number of teeth in the load gear to
the number of teeth in the __________.
questions.explanation:
In mechanical devices, gears are used to change torque.
The ideal mechanical advantage of a gear is the ratio of the number of teeth in the load gear to
the number of teeth in the effort gear.

questions.stem:
Which mechanical components are typically used between a wheel and an axle to reduce
friction?
questions.explanation:
A set of bearings is typically a set of small metal balls packed in a groove and lubricated with
grease or oil.
The wheel rubs against one side of each ball, and the axle rubs against the other side.



The net effect is that the wheel rolls much more easily.

questions.stem:
A block of steel has a density of 0.29 pounds per cubic inch.
If the block has dimensions of 1 inch by 1 inch by 3 inches, what is its weight?
questions.explanation:
The volume of the block can be calculated by multiplying its length by its width by its height, or 1
times 1 times 3, which equals 2 cubic inches.
The weight is the density multiplied by its volume, which is 3 cubic inches multiplied by 0.29
pounds per cubic inch, which equals 0.87 pounds.

questions.stem: Which principle of mechanical motion is used in the design of a roller coaster?
questions.explanation:
Acceleration must be considered in designing the maximum rise of the first hill.
Momentum must be considered to ensure the train gets back to the starting point, since it has
no motor.
Friction must be considered in the design of the braking system.

questions.stem: Which term below best describes the OPPOSITE of an increase in speed?
questions.explanation: Deceleration means slowing down.

questions.stem: A valve is used to perform which of the following functions?

options.A: increase the temperature of a liquid
options.B: control the flow of a liquid
options.D: decrease the density of a liquid

questions.explanation:
Valves are placed in piping systems and can be opened or closed in order to control the flow of
liquids or gasses.

questions.stem:
The sprocket on a bicycle is most similar to which of the simple mechanical devices listed
below?
questions.explanation:
A bicycle sprocket is the classic example of a gear, which is defined as a toothed wheel or
cylinder that meshes with a chain or with another toothed element to transfer energy or motion.

questions.stem: A pump is typically used to accomplish which of the following tasks?
questions.explanation:
Pumps are not used to move liquids downhill because liquids will flow downhill by gravity.
Also, pumps do not separate or clarify liquids; instead, they agitate and mix liquids.

questions.stem:
In the diagram shown above, the spring is very stiff and can be stretched 1 inch by a pulling
force of 100 pounds.
How much force must be applied to the block in order to move the box 3.5 inches to the left?
questions.explanation: 3.5 inches multiplied by 100 pounds per inch equals 350 pounds.

questions.stem:
A concrete beam has a maximum strength of 3,000 psi (pounds per square inch). In an
experiment, a 500- pound weight is placed in the center of the beam, and the stress in the beam
is measured to be 1,000 psi.
If the stresses in the beam continue to increase at the same rate with added weight, how much
additional weight can be added to the same location on the beam before the beam will break?
questions.explanation:
The first 500 pounds generated 1,000 psi of stress in the beam; therefore, 500 more pounds will
increase the
total stress to 2,000 psi.



Another 500 pounds will increase the stress to 3,000 psi, which we are told is the maximum
strength of the beam.
Therefore, the maximum additional load that can be applied to this beam before it breaks is
1,000 pounds.

questions.stem: An elevator is most similar to which of the following mechanical devices?
questions.explanation: An elevator is simply a crane that raises and lowers people.

questions.stem:
There are three beams that are each 10 feet long and all of the same size. One is made of
wood, another of steel, and the third of concrete.
If identical loads are applied to these three beams, which of the following will occur?

options.A: The steel beam will deflect less than the wood beam.
options.B: The wood beam will deflect less than the concrete beam.
options.C: The wood beam will deflect less than the steel beam.
options.D: The concrete beam will deflect more than the other two.

questions.explanation:
The steel beam will deflect less than the wood beam.
Choice "The steel beam will deflect less than the wood beam" is not correct since the concrete
beam will deflect less that the wood beam - concrete is stiffer than wood.

questions.stem: What mechanical motion principle do the brakes in a car or on a bicycle use?
questions.explanation:
When the brakes are applied, the brake pads rub on the wheel and the frictional force of this
rubbing slows down the vehicle.

questions.stem: The center of gravity of a baseball bat would be best described as __________.
questions.explanation: The center of gravity is the place on an object where there is equal weight on either side.

questions.stem: Which material is best suited for use as a boat anchor?
questions.explanation:
Foam and wood float and would therefore make poor boat anchors.
Glass is not strong enough to be used as a boat anchor.

questions.stem:
What would happen to a balloon full of air if you moved it from above a water surface to ten feet
below the water surface?

options.B: The volume of the balloon would decrease.
options.C: The volume of the balloon would increase.
options.D: The volume of the balloon would stay the same.

questions.explanation:
The volume of the balloon would decrease.
The pressure of the water would press inward on the balloon and cause it to shrink in volume.

questions.stem: What is Newton's Third Law of Motion?

options.A: What goes up must come down.
options.B: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
options.C: Reactions are a result of large actions.

questions.stem: The term equilibrium is defined as __________.

options.A: the state in which similar forces attract, causing a swell of movement in a single direction
options.B: the principle describing the notion that every action must have a reaction
options.C: the state in which opposing forces are balanced
options.D: the presence of motion in the present day which serves as a means of understanding movement as a whole

questions.stem: What is the definition and the danger of recoil?

options.A: To recoil is to move quickly and efficiently, and it is not dangerous but desired.
options.B: To recoil is to feel revolted or disgusted, and it is dangerous because it creates job dissatisfaction.
options.C: To recoil is to respond in fear, and it is dangerous because engineers and workers need to remain in control. Losing control could result in serious injuries on the job.
options.D: Recoil is the concept of "kicking back" or leaping back after being released. It may be dangerous due to the possibility of injury upon having equipment "leap back" rapidly.

questions.stem: Another word or phrase for false gravity is __________.
The phrase "to adopt power" means __________ when working.

options.A: to increase speed and efficiency to become your absolute best
options.B: to use a forceful tone when discussing work with a coworker
options.C: to focus energy on the lesser objects before moving on to larger instincts
options.D: to work authoritatively and with a slim, fit physique

questions.stem: A __________ should be applied if gear shafts are not parallel to one another.
What is the advantage of using wheels and axles?

options.A: Wheels and axles provide greater power, enabling workers to achieve greater results with less effort.
options.B: Wheels and axles are responsible for bearing the brunt of difficult lifting.
options.C: Wheels and axles are not beneficial.
options.D: Wheels and axles create a more effective conveyor belt effect.

questions.stem: What is the function of a vise in mechanical applications?

options.A: In mechanical applications, vises are used to arrest motion.
options.B: Vises are used to suspend quick movements, slowing the effects of conveyor belts.
options.C: In mechanical applications, vises are designed to assist movement.
options.D: Vises are designed to function as a source of stability, much like how legs function beneath a table.

questions.stem: A hydraulic jack performs the task of moving objects by __________.

options.A: utilizing oil; because oil cannot be compressed, pressure is placed upon the oil, resulting in a lifting motion
options.B: pressing together two interfacing parts to increase height
options.C: using a pulley system to lift items
options.D: using a corkscrew-like effect to function

questions.stem: Which of these statements about force is correct?

options.A: The amount of force required to move an object depends on the frictional forces between the object and its surroundings and must be calculated entirely based on individual situations.
options.B: The amount of force required to move an object does not depend on frictional conditions and cannot and will not exceed the weight of the object in question.
options.C: The amount of force required to move an object depends only on the weight of the object in question.
options.D: Force is best used in levered applications.

questions.stem: The purpose of mechanical comprehension is __________.

options.A: to inform workers on the proper use and function of machines
options.B: to determine how to adequately use mechanic's tools
options.C: to learn the use of various mechanisms
options.D: to describe the training undergone by car mechanics

questions.stem: What is the primary difference between distillation and evaporation?

options.A: Distillation separates or purifies liquids, while evaporation changes the form of a substance.
options.B: One is intentional in scope, while the other occurs during other practices.
options.C: Distillation involves the use of implements, while evaporation only requires heat.
options.D: Distillation and evaporation have no primary difference; they are the same process.

questions.stem: What is the state known as equilibrium?

options.A: Equilibrium describes the action of two similar forces coming together.
options.B: Equilibrium describes the state in which two different items possess equal force, resulting in balance.
options.C: Equilibrium describes the action of two opposing forces coming together in a crash.
options.D: Equilibrium describes the state created by the coming together of parallel forces.

questions.stem: What purpose does an inclined plane serve?

options.A: An inclined plane is a tilted surface designed to aid in supporting or transporting a load.
options.B: Inclined planes are not useful implements and have been replaced by more effective methods of transportation.
options.C: Inclined planes are tilted surfaces designed to assist in suspension.
options.D: An inclined plane is intended to aid only in unloading merchandise.

questions.stem:
If two workers are carrying a single load with the assistance of a board or plane, how should the
load be placed to ensure an entirely equitable division of effort?

options.A: The load should be placed the same length from one side as the load is long; i.e. if the load is 3 feet wide, it should be placed 3 feet from the edge of the plane.
options.B: The load should be placed directly in the middle of the board or plane to ensure equal labor division between workers.
options.C: The cargo should be held directly, rather than placing strain on a board or plane.
options.D: The load should be placed closer to one end to prevent bowing of the plane.

questions.stem:
A string of six gears exists, with each gear turning in conjunction with one another.
Which gears operate in the same rotation?
Which is the best description of centrifugal force?

options.A: the force responsible for the changes made to water during distillation.
options.B: the response of bodies with inertia to the straight-moving or curved behavior of their container.
options.C: the force by which bodies are propelled forward.
options.D: the relationship between two opposing forces.

questions.stem: What is the definition of a "concurrent force"?

options.A: A force system requiring concurrent movement.
options.B: A force system described as having multiple sources of force.
options.C: A system requiring all systems to pass through the same point.
options.D: A series of forces requiring simultaneous movement.

questions.stem: How does oil function in a machine with a series of moving parts?

options.A: Oil functions as a cleaning agent, allowing all moving parts to remain free of dirt and grime.
options.B: Oil functions as a source of lubrication, allowing moving parts to function as a single unit.

extreme force?

options.D: A pulley system, as might be found in warehouses and shipyards.

questions.stem: What determines the speed of a pulley system?

options.A: The material used as the belt (such as leather and rubber).
options.B: The size of the pulleys as a whole.
options.C: The size and ratio of all pulleys involved.
options.D: The length of the rope or belt used in the pulley system.

questions.stem:
Pulley systems require the synchronized movement of all pulleys.
How can pulleys escape this rule?

options.A: To violate this rule, pulley systems may be used in conjunction with gears.
options.B: This rule cannot be effectively violated.
options.C: To violate this rule, pulley system belts must be reversed.
options.D: Pulleys using twisted belts may move in opposing directions.

questions.stem: What are the three components of a lever?

options.B: A point of origin and solid plane
options.C: A wide plane, fulcrum, and effort arm
options.D: Fulcrum, resistance arm, and effort arm

questions.stem: What determines the speed of an output gear?

options.A: None of these (Gear speed is not capable of alteration.)
options.C: The speed of the input gear and the ratio of the number of teeth on each gear.

questions.stem: What are the potential functions of gear systems?

options.A: Gears may be used to change direction in machinery and can be used to increase speed.
options.B: Gears possess a single function: transmitting motion.
options.C: The potential functions of gears are: changes in direction, speed changes (both increases and decreases), and motion transmission.
options.D: Gears are primarily used for making changes in speed, but may also be used to instigate motion in machinery.

questions.stem: If a mechanical device is reported to have an advantage of 2, what does this mean?

options.A: The number "2" describes the effectiveness of the machine.
options.B: This means the device allows users to complete twice the amount of work with the same amount of effort used to complete a task without assistance.
options.C: The number refers to the speed of the device in question.
options.D: This means that the device requires twice the amount of effort to complete the same amount of work.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a Class 1 Lever?
questions.explanation:
Pliers are an example of a Class 1 lever (actually 2 class 1 levers).
Wheelbarrow and stapler are class 2. Tongs are class 3.

options.A: The air remains at the same temperature

questions.explanation: Air is a gas. According to the gas laws, gasses will get colder when they contract.

questions.stem: Which of the following would feel hottest at one end if the other end were placed over a fire?
questions.explanation:
Of the four materials, metal is the best conductor of heat, so a metal skewer would feel the
hottest.

questions.stem:
If you use a lever to lift a 200 pound weight with an effort of 40 pounds, with is the mechanical
advantage?
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = load/effort = 200/40 = 5

questions.stem:
Water flows into a container at a rate of 140 gallons per minute. The container has a small
opening at the bottom that drains water at a rate of 1 gallon per second.
How long will it take to fill the container to 240 gallons?
questions.explanation:
The opening drains water at 1 gallon/second which is equivalent to 60 gallons/min.



Therefore, the net gain of water is 140 gallons/min - 60/gallons/min = 80 gallons/min.
To fill 240 gallons at a rate of 80 gallons/min will take 3 minutes.

questions.stem:
Which of the following statements is true for water flowing from a 4 inch pipe to a smaller 2 inch
pipe?

options.A: The same amount of water passes through both the 4 inch pipe and the 2 inch pipe.
options.B: The pressure is greater in the 2 inch pipe.
options.C: More water passes through the 4 inch pipe than through the 2 inch pipe.
options.D: The pressure is lower in the 4 inch pipe.

questions.explanation:
Water cannot be compressed. Therefore, the same amount of water must be flowing through
both the 4 inch pipe and the 2 inch pipe.

questions.stem: What is the mechanical advantage of this pulley system?
questions.explanation:
In a pulley system, you calculate the mechanical advantage by counting up the number of
supporting ropes/ strands that support the weight.
In this case, there are 3 supporting strands that support the load, so the mechanical advantage
is 3.

questions.stem: In the figure below, if gear A turns 15 times, how many revolutions will gear B make?
questions.explanation:
Gear A has 18 teeth and gear B has 6 teeth.
Therefore, for every 1 revolution of gear A, gear B will have 3 revolutions.

questions.stem:
Pulling on the rope at point A will lift the load.
How far will you have to pull the rope at point A to lift the load 15 feet?
questions.explanation:
The mechanical advantage of the pulley is 3 since there are three ropes supporting the load.
Therefore, the distance at point A needs to 3x or 3 × 15 = 45 ft.

questions.stem:
In the figure below, if gear 1 turns counterclockwise (as shown by the arrow), which of the gears
will also turn in the same direction?
questions.explanation:
Gear 1 turns counterclockwise causing gear 2 to turn clockwise which results in gear 3 and 4 to
turn counterclockwise.

questions.stem: In the pulley system below, how fast does pulley D rotate, if pulley A rotates at 50 rpm?
questions.explanation:
A larger pulley causes a smaller pulley to rotate faster by the ratio of their diameters.
If pulley A rotates at 50 rpm, then pulley B rotates at 50 × 8/5=80 rpm.
Since C is directly connected to B it rotates at the same rate (80 rpm).
Finally, pulley D will rotate at 80 rpm x 10/4 = 200 rpm

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a Class 2 Lever?
questions.explanation:
A bottle opener is a single class 2 lever.
A see-saw and scissors are class 1 levers.
A Fishing rod is a class 3 lever.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a type of simple machine?
questions.explanation:
The six types of simple machines are: pulley, lever, screw, wheel and axle, wedge, inclined
plane.

questions.stem: In the pulley system below, how fast does pulley D rotate, if pulley A rotates at 100 rpm?
questions.explanation:
A larger pulley causes a smaller pulley to rotate faster by the ratio of their diameters.
If pulley A rotates at 100 rpm, then pulley B rotates at 100 × 4/10 = 40 rpm.
Since C is directly connected to B it rotates at the same rate (40 rpm).
Finally, pulley D will rotate at 40 rpm × 5/16 = 12.5 rpm

questions.stem: What weight (X) is needed to balance the two loads shown in the figure below?
questions.explanation:
For the weights to balance, the sum of the forces must balance.
Therefore, (5 lbs × 8 ft) + (10 lbs × 4 ft) = X lbs × 8 ft or 40 lb-ft + 40 lb-ft =8X lb-ft or X=10 lbs

questions.stem:
The diagram below represents a load sliding down an incline.
Which of the forces (A,B,C, or D) represent friction?
questions.explanation: Friction is represented by the force the resists the load moving down the hill.

questions.stem:
On a bicycle there are 30 teeth on the gear sprocket connected to the pedals, and 10 teeth on
the sprocket connected to the rear wheels.
If you pedal the bike 12 times, how many times will the rear wheel turn?
questions.explanation:
Since there are 30 teeth on the pedal sprocket, but only 10 teeth on the rear wheel, each
revolution of the pedal will turn the rear wheel 3 times.
So 12 revolutions will turn the rear wheel 36 times.

questions.stem: An axe is an example of what type of simple machine.
questions.explanation: An axe is a classic example of a wedge.

questions.stem: When a football is thrown upwards in the air, what causes it to arc back towards the ground?
questions.explanation:
Gravity is the force that causes objects to be pulled back towards the earth.
